output: Manchester City captain Vincent Kompany criticizes UEFA's Financial Fair Play (FFP) regulations, arguing they protect established clubs rather than preventing financial collapse. City, despite being debt-free, were fined £50 million last year for FFP violations, while Manchester United spent £150 million on new talent despite being in debt. Kompany believes FFP prevents lesser teams from challenging the established elite. He also commends the impact of City's owners on the community and the city of Manchester, claiming that without their investment, a top-level club might not have been possible under stringent FFP rules.

Bath has signed England Sevens international Jeff Williams for the upcoming season. The 26-year-old, who has bypassed 36 tries on the World Series circuit, will join the team from the Recreation Ground. Williams, a South Africa native whose father is English, previously played for the Hamiltons club in Cape Town and had a stint in France. Bath's head coach, Mike Ford, is excited about Williams' dynamism and high-tempo playing style, which will fit the team's attacking ethos. England Sevens head coach Simon Amor lauds Williams' contributions to the squad, including his physicality and development as a player.

1. On Friday, director David Ayer released the first full-look image of Jared Leto as the Joker in the upcoming film "Suicide Squad", with the movie set to release on August 5, 2016.
2. Leto, who won an Oscar for his role in "Dallas Buyers Club", underwent a dramatic transformation for the role, appearing as the popular DC Comics villain first introduced by Heath Ledger in 2008's "The Dark Knight".
3. In addition to Leto, the upcoming movie featuring a group of anti-heroes includes notable actors like Will Smith, Margot Robbie, and a large ensemble cast, with the Joker notably appearing alongside them in the absence of Batman.

Three Florida corrections officers and a former trainee have been charged by Florida's Attorney General for conspiring to murder a former inmate, reportedly due to a prior altercation. An FBI informant infiltrated the Traditional American Knights of the Ku Klux Klan to investigate, after which the three men expressed satisfaction when shown a staged homicide scene of the target by the FBI. If convicted, each could face up to 30 years in prison for conspiracy to commit murder. Statewide Prosecutor Nick Cox commented on the men's happiness over the staged crime scene, emphasizing Florida's zero-tolerance policy towards hate-driven violence.

The conference call between Manny Pacquiao and Floyd Mayweather, scheduled to discuss their upcoming boxing fight, was abruptly cancelled due to technical difficulties caused by a high number of participating boxing writers and broadcasters. Pacquiao was only able to answer one question about his training camp, with the call being rescheduled due to the large number of callers not being able to connect. American boxer Floyd Mayweather is expected to address the media during his own conference call on Wednesday.

The Miami Open has seen a trend of celebration cakes for notable tennis victories, with Serena Williams receiving one for her 700th career win and Andy Murray for his 500th. Williams advanced to the semi-finals by defeating Sabine Lisicki in three sets, avenging her 2013 Wimbledon loss to the German player. In another match, Simona Halep defeated Sloane Stephens to secure a semi-final match against Williams.

1. Beijing International Airport, commonly known as Daxing Airport, is building the world's largest terminal, Terminal 1, to accommodate the rising number of Chinese tourists traveling globally. The terminal, set to open in 2018, will span 700,000 square metres and cater to 45 million passengers annually.

2. Renowned architect Zaha Hadid collaborated with ADPI on the terminal's design, aiming for an open and spacious layout with minimal obstructions like columns, epitomizing the harmony between Chinese landscape and culture. The terminal will feature a central multi-layered courtyard as a meeting place for globally diverse passengers.

3. The new terminal, firmly positioning Beijing on the global stage, will reportedly manage wide open spaces, facilitated by the lack of pillars and a flowing roof design, marking a significant response to research showing a dramatic increase in the number of Chinese tourists, from 10 million in 2000 to 109 million in 2014, spending over $164 billion.

1. Manchester United manager Louis van Gaal revealed that Wayne Rooney sustained a knee injury during their defeat by Everton on Sunday; the England international was replaced by Robin van Persie in the closing stages of the game.
2. The severe nature of Rooney's injury remains uncertain, with Van Gaal stating they would have to wait and see.
3. The defeat leaves United fourth in the Premier League, and in potential danger of losing their automatic Champions League qualification spot, with Liverpool now applying pressure due to their improved form.

Jack Wilshere, despite being on Manchester City's transfer list, is recovering from ankle surgery and preparing to return to Arsenal's first team. During a day off, he shared a photo on Instagram of his shopping haul, which included cereals, eggs, baked beans, and corn on the cob. Wilshere humorously requested help from his followers to put away his groceries after his shopping spree.

A Venezuelan woman, Marleni Olivo, threw a mango at President Nicolas Maduro during a rally, hoping to get his attention for her housing issue. Instead, Maduro publicly announced on live TV that he would provide her with a new apartment as part of his Great Housing Mission. Olivo claimed her action was not meant to harm Maduro but to express her desire for a home. Critics have dubbed the incident a "manguicidio," a play on the words "mango" and "magnicidio," a term meaning assassination of a powerful leader, but Olivo denies any malicious intent.

Carlos Tevez, a former striker for Manchester United and City and currently playing for Juventus, claims it is more challenging to score goals in Serie A than the Premier League due to stronger defending and a less active midfield. He states that in the Italian league, strikers often face five defenders, contrasting with the dynamic, goal-friendly environment of the Premier League. Despite sitting out a recent loss to Parma, Tevez maintains his goal-scoring task is harder in Italy and believes his current team, Juventus, has the potential to rival Manchester United's 2008 Champions League victory, citing their strong overall teamwork.

Jamie Carragher, Sky Sports columnist, accused Manchester City's Yaya Toure of shying away from his duties during a free-kick for Crystal Palace, which resulted in the winning goal that effectively ended City's hope for a comeback at Selhurt Park. Toure reportedly ducked when the ball was struck, despite being part of a five-man wall, and Carragher criticized this behavior, stating it was not acceptable for a player of Toure's stature. This defeat left City nine points behind leaders Chelsea, who also have a game in hand.

A 50-year-old Australian man, believed to be from Seymour in Victoria, died suddenly on Wednesday while on holiday in Kuta, Bali. He collapsed in the Rooftop Restaurant at the 101 Legian Hotel after telling a waitress he wasn't feeling well. Kuta, a popular destination for Australian tourists, is known for its long sandy beach, varied accommodations, and numerous restaurants and bars. An autopsy is pending to determine the exact cause of death, but external examinations suggest it was likely a heart attack.

Richie Benaud, a former Australia cricket captain and commentator, died last week at the age of 84 from skin cancer complications. His private funeral service was held in Sydney on Wednesday and was attended by ex-players Shane Warne and Ian Chappell, as well as close family and friends. Despite an offer of a state funeral from Australian Prime Minister Tony Abbott, Benaud's family opted for a smaller service at the Eastern Suburbs Memorial Park. Benaud's career spanned from his test debut in January 1952 to his final commentary in England in September 2005. He is considered one of the most influential cricket identities of the past century, known for his distinctive voice and commentary style.

A 16-year-old named Isobel Attwood has been missing for two days. She is believed to be with a man in his twenties, potentially in Southampton. The police are appealing for help and express concern for her welfare. Isobel has posted on social media saying she is safe but needs some time away, and friends suggest she is with her boyfriend. The police urge anyone with information regarding her whereabouts to contact them.

Manchester City faces a £12 million loss in bonuses for failing to qualify for the Champions League, as player contracts are incentivized to meet financial fairplay rules. After a loss to Manchester United, City is now in fourth place, four points ahead of Liverpool, who could potentially claim the final Champions League spot. city manager Manuel Pellegrini admits the team has performed poorly in recent months, impacting their ability to attract top talent like Paul Pogba, who is also a target for United.

Martin Skrtel, Liverpool defender, has denied rumors of a move away from the club, citing his intention to stay despite his contract ending in 2016. He has been linked with a transfer to both Wolfsburg and Napoli, but his agent has confirmed that there is currently an offer on the table for a contract extension with Liverpool, and no serious interest from Wolfsburg. Skrtel played in Liverpool's 2-1 FA Cup semi-final loss to Aston Villa on Sunday.

A CEO named Cheryl Rios, from Texas, has received criticism for stating on her Facebook page that biology prevents a woman from being president due to hormones. The comments followed Hillary Clinton's announcement of her presidential run. Rios, though supporting equal rights, believes there's biblical reasoning against a woman presidency and faced backlash on social media as people labeled her comments as misogynistic and hypocritical. Rios, amid criticism, maintained that her views aren't abusive and oppressive towards women, and she has the right to her opinions.

In the first leg of the Champions League quarter-final between Atletico Madrid and Real Madrid, striker Mario Mandzukic sustained a cut to his nose and a punch to his stomach during a physical encounter. Despite these injuries, Manager Diego Simeone expects Mandzukic to be fit for the return leg at the Bernabeu on Wednesday. Mandzukic is favored to play alongside Antoine Griezmann in attack, with the latter in excellent form after scoring both goals in their recent La Liga match.

1. Jose Mourinho, Chelsea's manager, had spent the week preparing his team to counteract Manchester United's Marouane Fellaini, only to find out from a hotel doorman that it was Fellaini's twin brother (Mansour) who was present, not the actual player.
2. Mourinho's plan involved player Kurt Zouma man-marking Fellaini, with Ruben Loftus-Cheek playing the part of Fellaini in training.
3. Despite the initial confusion, Fellaini did play in the actual game at Stamford Bridge, where Chelsea won 1-0, and Zouma was tasked with containing him, contributing to Chelsea's potential two more wins needed to secure the Premier League title.

A New Jersey woman named Dawn Milosky was rescued from her overturned and smoking car just before it caught fire, following a tip-off about erratic driving in Kinnelon. Officers Mark Ehrenberg and Ricky Ferriola arrived on scene, discovered Milosky unconscious, and managed to pull her from the vehicle in less than 3 minutes. The car was engulfed in flames approximately 30 seconds later. Milosky survived with injuries and was identified. She has been charged with driving while intoxicated, having an open container of alcohol in the vehicle, reckless driving, and failure to stay in the right lane. Despite the serious incident, she is reportedly doing okay following hospitalization.

A farmer in eastern China, Xiao Qibin, has a six-legged goat named the 'spider goat' by Chinese web users. The goat was born with four forelegs and two hind legs roughly 20 days ago, and despite initial doubts about its survival, it is growing quickly and has an extraordinary appetite. Xiao takes care of the goat, which has become one of the most playful animals on his farm, and has decided not to remove the extra legs, instead wanting the goat to grow up naturally.

1. West Ham United are considering a move for Javier Hernandez, who scored a crucial goal for Real Madrid against Atletico Madrid, as part of their summer recruitment strategy.
2. Hernandez, currently on loan from Manchester United at Real Madrid, is not in Louis van Gaal's plans and could be acquired for approximately £7 million.
3. In addition to Hernandez, West Ham have identified Sampdoria's Pedro Obiang, FC Sion's Moussa Konate, and Basle's Fabian Schar as primary transfer targets ahead of their final season at Upton Park.

Stuart McCall, the manager of Scottish football club Rangers, has dismissed any speculation about his future being decided before the end of the season. He has been credited with restoring a positive atmosphere at the club, with three consecutive wins, including victories over Hibs and Hearts. McCall believes his side has not yet achieved anything significant in the Championship and is focusing on the upcoming game against Queen of the South. Shane Ferguson, a loan signing from Newcastle United, is set to join Rangers next week, two months after the initial deal, but McCall is unsure how quickly Ferguson can return to match fitness after a long-term injury.

In a crucial match, Werder Bremen defeated Hamburg SV 1-0 with a late penalty by Franco Di Santo, keeping their hopes for a Europa League spot alive. Di Santo converted the penalty in the 84th minute, and Hamburg's Valon Behrami received a red card for bringing down Zlatko Junuzovic. Hamburg remains in last place, while Werder moved up to seventh position. Meanwhile, second-placed VfL Wolfsburg aims to reduce Bayern Munich's lead to 10 points when they take on Schalke 04 later on the same day, with Bayern currently at the top after their 2-0 win over Hoffenheim. Bayer Leverkusen is in third place following their 4-0 triumph over Hanover 96.

A two-year-old boy fell about 10-12 feet into a cheetah exhibit at the Cleveland Metroparks Zoo after his parents dangled him over the railing. The child was rescued by his parents before emergency services arrived and sustained minor injuries. The zoo plans to press child endangering charges against the family, with the exhibit being closed following the incident. A witness at the scene expressed shock and disbelief at the parents' actions.

A Russian TV channel gave Hillary Clinton's campaign video a mature audience rating due to fears it may violate the country's anti-gay propaganda law. The rating was given due to scenes showing a gay couple holding hands, a moment from the video that lasted about five seconds. The law, passed in 2013 and criticized internationally, bans discussion of gay rights and relationships in the presence of minors, causing controversy and international outcry, including a boycott of the 2014 Winter Olympics in Sochi.

Dutch midfielder Siem de Jong returned from a collapsed lung to play 45 minutes for Newcastle Under 21s, but his comeback was cut short at halftime in a 2-0 loss to Derby County. De Jong has seen limited playing time since his transfer from Ajax last year. Despite the setback, he might have a chance to appear in the final six matches this season. Derby won the game with goals from Alefe Santos and Farrend Rawson. Meanwhile, Facundo Ferreyra, a loaned-in Argentinian striker who has yet to make his senior debut due to injuries, took De Jong's place at halftime.

A chef named Ally Lees from Alfie Bird's restaurant in Birmingham created a giant omelette containing 150 eggs and 12,000 calories, featuring 945g of protein, which is 16 times the daily recommended amount for a man. The omelette, which is approximately three-foot in circumference, would require more than five people to eat. The dish was prepared as a festive promotion for Easter and took an hour to cook using a giant paella pan. It's recommended that at least five people attempt to consume this large omelette, but the chef himself admits it might be challenging due to the excess protein content.

This summer, the Sainsbury's Anniversary Games will feature three Olympic gold medalists: Jessica Ennis-Hill (heptathlon), Mo Farah (10,000 meters), and Greg Rutherford (long jump). These athletes won their gold medals during the Super Saturday event at the 2012 London Olympics, and Ennis-Hill will be making her first appearance since giving birth last summer. The event will take place at the Olympic Stadium from July 24-26, featuring a two-day Diamond League meeting and the Sainsbury's IPC Athletics Grand Prix Final. Tickets for the event are now on sale, with prices starting from £20 per adult and £12 for concessions on July 24-25 and £10 on July 26. The event is expected to attract a large crowd, with the hope of recreating the atmosphere of the 2013 Anniversary Games.

1. Police in Rio de Janeiro found evidence that a snack bar was using the meat of stray dogs to make traditional Brazilian pastries, filled with ground beef, instead.

2. The owner, Chinese Van Ruilonc, confessed to rounding up strays from the streets and using them as sources of meat, while also allegedly exploiting Chinese workers in slave-like conditions.

3. A public prosecutor expressed shock at the discovery, describing finding the frozen dog carcasses as "worse than everything" and reporting the presence of a cell-like jail within the snack bar, where a worker was held and forced to work long hours without pay.

The article discusses the case of Ebony Dickens, who posted violent threats against white police officers on Facebook under a fake name, Tiffany Milan. The threats lead authorities to arrest Dickens, who was charged with disseminating information related to terrorist acts. During a search of Dickens' residence, a firearm and three computers were found. Dickens was released on a $10,000 bond and banned from social media.

PSV Eindhoven won the Dutch championship for the first time in seven seasons after a 4-1 victory over Heerenveen, with key contributions from striker Luuk de Jong, Memphis Depay, and Luciano Narsingh. Meanwhile, bottom side Dordrecht moved closer to relegation after a 3-0 loss at Vitesse Arnhem, and AZ Alkmaar secured a spot in the Europa League playoffs.

An 11-year-old boy named Shiva was reportedly beaten to death by his school head teacher, Lalit Verma, for stealing another student's pencil and eraser in Railamau village, India. The alleged assault led to internal bleeding and Shiva's death upon arrival at Fatehpur Hospital. Lalit Verma has been charged with culpable homicide not amounting to murder. This incident follows previous reports of extreme corporal punishment by teachers, leading to the death of young boys, such as a nine-year-old in Burdwan, West Bengal, beaten with a stick, and a boy in Bareilly, Uttar Pradesh, who was thrown out of a window onto a busy road due to unpaid school fees.

A gastrointestinal illness has affected over 100 passengers and crew on the Celebrity Infinity cruise ship, with symptoms including vomiting and diarrhea. The Centers for Disease Control (CDC) is investigating the cause of the illness and plans to meet the ship in San Diego on Monday. The Celebrity Infinity has previously experienced similar outbreaks in 2006 and 2013.

A Boston Terrier named Gizmo has gained popularity online by performing a unique trick known as paw-stand walking, where he walks on his front legs while his back legs are elevated vertically. This unusual trick was recorded by his owner, Loren Mathieson, after Gizmo tried on new black boots and appeared unsure about how to walk in them. The video of the gravity-defying trick has garnered over 80,000 views and brought smiles to many viewers' faces.

New Orleans, known for its lively nightlife and celebrations, implemented a city-wide smoking ban on bars, casinos, and restaurants, effective from midnight on Tuesdays, due to concerns about secondhand smoke affecting workers. The unanimous decision by the New Orleans City Council faced opposition from bar owners and regular customers, with some taking legal action to challenge the ban. This ban, however, doesn't affect popular tourist activities like experiencing Treme or enjoying a beignet.

Manchester United's Under 21 team, captained by Adnan Januzaj, secured a 3-1 victory against West Ham United to go four points clear at the top of the Under 21 Premier League. West Ham took an early lead through Reece Oxford but responded quickly with Josh Harrop scoring twice by capitalizing on poor goalkeeping from the opposition. Despite some pressure from West Ham, the young Red Devils held on to claim all three points.

1. Brisbane's Anglican Archbishop, Phillip Aspinall, has joined a local Catholic priest in advocating for the removal of Queensland's 'gay panic' homicide defense, which reduces murder charges to manslaughter if the defendant claims their victim made an unwanted advance.

2. In a talk after an Easter Sunday mass, Archbishop Aspinall expressed his support for this initiative, emphasizing that self-defense should not include violence in response to unwanted sexual advances. He also addressed issues of violence at recent anti-Islam rallies and church vandalism.

3. Archbishop Aspinall further appealed to his followers to resist reacting out of fear and to honor the spirit of resurrection in their everyday lives, ultimately promoting peace and understanding.

Sandra Bullock, aged 50, has been named the world's most beautiful woman of 2015 by People magazine, joining a list that includes Lupita Nyong'o (2014) and Gwyneth Paltrow (2013). Bullock, in a humble response, calls the award "ridiculous" and emphasizes that true beauty lies in being a good person, a good mother, and not seeking superficial appearance ideals. The cover story for the magazine focuses on Bullock's home life with her son, Louis, 5, and her personal journey to maintain health and fitness post-40. Reactions to her selection, particularly by fans, highlight her enduring beauty and talent at over 50 years of age, as Bullock herself asserts, "I can look in the mirror and like who I see." Other notable names in this year's "most beautiful" list include Gabrielle Union, Ariana Grande, and Laverne Cox.

An improvised bomb exploded near a U.N. vehicle in Garowe, northeastern Somalia on Monday, killing six people, including four UNICEF aid workers. President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud called the attack an attack on the future of Somalia. Al-Shabaab, a terrorist group based in Somalia, claimed responsibility for the bombing. This incident follows a separate ambush on Sunday in the Lower Shabelle region where three African Union troops died.

A wildlife park operator named Gary Saurage, resembling a modern-day Crocodile Dundee, was called to capture a 400-pound, 11-foot alligator from a family's backyard pond in Beaumont, Texas. The image captured during the capture shows Saurage approaching the aggressive creature with bare hands, looking directly into the alligator's eyes. After successful removal, Saurage revealed the alligator, estimated to be between 35 to 40 years old, was later confirmed male and brought to his park, where it joined over 400 other alligators. Saurage emphasized that while alligators can be dangerous, they are manageable as long as people maintain a safe distance and refrain from feeding them, given their speed and hunting abilities.

In a clash in eastern Turkey, five Kurdistan Workers' Party militants were killed and another wounded, while four Turkish soldiers were wounded. The violence occurred in Agri city as Turkish forces were securing an area ahead of a spring festival, and was condemned by Turkish Prime Minister Ahmet Davutoglu and President Recep Tayyip Erdogan. The Kurdish separatist conflict, ongoing for more than three decades, has resulted in tens of thousands of lives lost, with Kurdish activists seeking independence while others view it as a guerrilla war with terrorist acts. The longtime leader of the Kurdistan Workers' Party, Abdullah Ocalan, recently called for an end to the violence from prison, urging followers to lay down their arms and join a "congress" to focus on the future.

Two 18-month-old twin boys were pronounced dead at a hospital following an accident where they fell in a canal in Yuma, Arizona. The incident occurred at 9.45am on Friday, and the area is commonly used for walks and jogging. Investigators believe the boys ended up in the canal by accident and do not suspect foul play. The rescue operation involved the Yuma Fire Department, U.S. Border Patrol, and the U.S. Marine Corps, with the boys eventually being flown to the hospital by the latter. Unfortunately, their efforts were unsuccessful, and the boys passed away.

Orlando City, an MLS team with a significant Latin-American fanbase, have shown interest in signing Javier Hernandez, a Mexican international who is currently on loan at Real Madrid but has faced struggles. Meanwhile, Manchester United are looking to retain midfielder Andreas Pereira, as several European clubs, including Paris St Germain, Juventus, PSV Eindhoven, and Feyenoord, are interested if he does not accept a new contract offer at United.

Joel Burger, 24, and Ashley King, 23, got engaged, favoring a humorous nickname given to them in fifth grade as "Burger King." They plan to celebrate their marriage with a creative twist, using personalized Burger King cups for drinks at their wedding. The couple met in kindergarten, became more than friends during college years, and are fond of the continual teasing from their friends regarding their unique names.

A hit band from the 1960s, unnamed in the article, is linked to a notorious paedophile brothel in Battersea, South West London, along with the disgraced BBC star Jimmy Savile. This information is from a secret police intelligence report from 1964, with no confirmation if they attended the brothel at the same time. The brothel was investigated in 2013 by Detective Superintendent David Grey when it was mentioned in another police report, but there is no evidence to suggest a direct connection or reason for further investigation besides hindsight.

A six-year-old German Shepherd named Sadie, adopted from an animal rescue shelter, was filmed playing an electric keyboard at her home in Alberta, Canada. She demonstrated a brief and unconventional performance that appeared to consist of minimalist, clashing notes with no discernible time signature. The footage showed Sadie using her paws to play the keys while sitting on a piano stool. The video of Sadie's unique performance has been widely praised on social media, with viewers commending both her musical skill and cuteness.

A 22-year-old man named Ivan Balashov, while shopping for phones in Novokuznetsk, Russia, took a selfie with a phone he found unappealing, then stole another one. He was caught when the shop identified him from the selfie. He denied being in the shop but was later found guilty and given a three-month suspended sentence.

The first trailer for a documentary titled "Amy: The Girl Behind the Name" about the life and music of late British singer Amy Winehouse was released, set for UK release on July 3. Winehouse, known for her struggle with drugs and alcohol, discusses her ambivalence towards fame in the trailer, expressing concern about the impact of celebrity on her mental health. The documentary is endorsed by Winehouse's family, featuring extensive unseen archive footage and previously unheard tracks, and has been filmed by Asif Kapadia, the director of the BAFTA-winning documentary "Senna." A U.S. release date for the film has yet to be announced.

This week, "The Big Bang Theory" (Thursday 8 p.m. ET, CBS) is a must-watch with the return of Christine Baranski and Laurie Metcalf as the mothers of Leonard and Sheldon. "Saturday Night Live" (Saturday May 2 at 11:30 p.m., NBC) features Scarlett Johannsson as host. "Mom" (Thursday 9:30 p.m., CBS) is concluding its season with Allison Janney delivering Emmy-worthy performances. "Backstrom" (Thursday 9 p.m., Fox) is airing its season finale for its quirky crime drama. "Blue Bloods" (Friday 10 p.m., CBS) is concluding its two-part season finale, although its future is uncertain. "Younger" (Tuesday 10 p.m., TV Land), a charming comedy, has been renewed for a second season, making this a great time to tune in.

The Downton Abbey character Violet, Countess of Grantham, played by Dame Maggie Smith, may return in a new series created by Julian Fellowes called The Gilded Age, set in the high society of New York in the late 19th century. The potential return of Robert, Earl of Grantham, and his wife Cora, who is American-born, is also hinted at, with Violet appearing as a younger character. NBC is currently excited about the production of The Gilded Age, aiming to recreate the grandeur of Downton Abbey with a focus on New York's wealthy robber barons. The sixth and final series of Downton Abbey airs later this year on ITV.

Steven Gerrard, who is finishing his career at Liverpool this season and moving to LA Galaxy, is set to start in Sunday's FA Cup semi-final at Wembley. He will replace the spot he's been missing due to a three-match suspension. Gerrard, a key player for Liverpool, has won previous trophies including the League Cup in 2012 and the FA Cup in 2006, and manager Brendan Rodgers is confident that Gerrard is ready to contribute significantly to the team once again.

A new, original Dr. Seuss book titled "What Pet Should I Get?" is set to be released on July 28, with pre-orders exceeding expectations. The book, featuring the spirited siblings from "One Fish Two Fish Red Fish Blue Fish," was penned between 1958 and 1962, and its manuscript and illustrations were found in Geisel's home shortly after his death in 1991. Random House Children's Books anticipates releasing more books from discovered materials.

Jessica Carey, upon visiting her grandmother after a three-hour drive, revealed a tattoo of a portrait of her grandmother as a young woman, eliciting an emotional reaction. The tattoo, created by her husband Aaron, was based on a childhood photograph of Patty Lawing, featuring long red hair and a smart outfit. To enhance the surprise, Jessica had also brought her two children along. The heartwarming moment was captured on film and has recently emerged online, showing Patty's obvious delight and gratitude.

Annegret Raunigk, a 65-year-old mother-of-13 from Berlin, is preparing to give birth to quadruplets in a matter of weeks, making her the oldest woman in the world to have quadruplets. Despite undergoing 18 months of fertility treatment and approaching retirement, Raunigk feels fit and not overly concerned about the upcoming birth. The father's identity remains unknown, and Raunigk previously made headlines in Germany for giving birth to her youngest daughter at the age of 55.

Japan's space agency, JAXA, has announced plans to launch an unmanned rover on the moon by 2018, joining an exclusive group of nations with lunar exploration. The mission, called SLIM (Smart Lander for Investigating Moon), is expected to cost between $83.4 million and $125 million. Its purpose includes perfecting soft-landing technologies, which may be applied to future human missions. The craft is planned to use a repurposed form of face recognition software, enabling it to recognize craters on the surface. The decision could be seen as a response to China and India's recent significant extraterrestrial achievements. Previous lunar missions by Japan include the SELENE (or Kaguya) craft in 2008.

1. Brazilian football clubs have imposed precautions amid a surge of dengue fever cases, as three players have been diagnosed with the mosquito-borne disease, including Corinthians striker Paolo Guerrero, forcing them to miss crucial matches.
2. With no cure for dengue fever, players have resorted to using insect repellent during practices and inspections for mosquito breeding sites, while the health ministry reports over 460,000 cases and more than 130 fatalities in 2015.
3. The outbreak has affected not only players but also staff members, such as Palmeiras reserve goalkeeper Aranha, who has also been diagnosed with dengue fever, causing concern among numerous top-tier Brazilian clubs.

James Wilson, a striker for Manchester United, expressed his admiration for teammate Wayne Rooney's ability to take free-kicks, revealing he would like to incorporate that skill into his own game. He also admired Robin van Persie's movement and Radamel Falcao's predatory instincts in the 18-yard box, aspiring to emulate those qualities. During his 16 appearances for United this season, Wilson has scored one Premier League goal.

A 2-year-old child was struck and killed by a van in Milwaukee, Wisconsin. The driver, identified as Archie Brown Jr., was then shot dead at the scene, potentially as an act of revenge. A 15-year-old boy also died from gunshot wounds, though the connection to the incident is unclear. Police are currently searching for the suspect, with local alderman Joe Davis suggesting that the shooting may have been in retaliation for the child's death. Brown Jr. was a father-of-four, a real estate entrepreneur, and co-owner of Seven West nightclub, leaving behind four daughters.

A minor boy from Memphis, Tennessee, has gained over 3,000 Twitter followers with posts featuring him posing with guns, drugs, and explicit language, prompting criticism from community members. Despite the backlash, the boy defends himself, claiming he's had a tough year and the criticism is stressing his mother. The boy's actions, as observed by local resident Orrden Williams, could lead to negative outcomes for society in the future. Authorities are aware of social media's role in perpetuating gang culture, with around 50% of organized gangs maintaining a social media presence in the United States.

1. Former Redgum frontman John Schumann firmly denounced anti-Islam protesters for using his song "I Was Only 19" during a Reclaim Australia rally, stating that the song promotes messages of compassion, tolerance, and inclusiveness.

2. Saturday's Reclaim Australia protests, which aimed to oppose 'sharia law, halal tax, and Islamization', led to violence in various cities across Australia when protesters clashed with anti-racism groups.

3. The controversy surrounding the misuse of Schumann's song prompted him to issue a statement, with the songwriter expressing his disappointment that his work was co-opted by a group promoting ignorance and intolerance.

Emmanuel Adebayor, Tottenham striker, has publicly stated his intention to stay with the team and fight for his place, disregarding transfer speculation. Despite an underwhelming performance against Sheffield United and a significant decline in form since his 2011 arrival, Adebayor remains optimistic and ambitious to remain with Tottenham, as his utilization in the team is limited due to the rise of homegrown star Harry Kane. Adebayor's most recent goal in the Premier League for Tottenham was during a 1-2 loss against Newcastle in October 2017, and he has made ten appearances this season, scoring only twice.

1. Manuel Pellegrini, the manager of Manchester City, is being urged by Stuart Pearce to be given more time to turn around the club's struggling fortunes, despite a poor run of form that has put the team in danger of missing out on Champions League qualification.

2. Pearce, a former player and manager at the club, believes that poor performance is due in part to the inconsistent form of Yaya Toure, and that the club should focus on freshening up the squad rather than replacing the manager.

3. Pearce also highlighted the efforts of Sergio Aguero as a bright spot in an otherwise underperforming Manchester City squad.

Hull City manager Steve Bruce remains optimistic about keeping Hull City in the Premier League despite a 2-0 loss to Southampton, targeting 8-9 wins to survive in the remaining games. The team had a strong start but injuries to key players like Michael Dawson, Nikica Jelavic, and Robert Snodgrass have affected their performance and left them just two points above the relegation zone. Manager Bruce attributed their struggles to these long-term injuries. Meanwhile, Southampton moved up to fifth place after James Ward-Prowse's penalty and Graziano Pelle's late goal. Manager Ronald Koeman faced his own issue when Sadio Mane attempted to take a penalty instead of Ward-Prowse, and he plans to speak with the team about respecting team rules.

A terror alert was triggered in Reading, UK after a dummy wearing a balaclava and holding a fake missile launcher was spotted on a boat sailing down the Thames. Thames Valley Police and an Army bomb disposal team were called, but after inspecting the missile, they determined it was purely ornamental. A local resident condemned the prank, expressing concern about the potential for panic and stressing the inappropriate timing given the recent terrorist activities.

Tiger Woods suffered a bizarre injury during the Masters tournament on Sunday, hitting a tree root with his club, causing a painful yelp, and briefly popping a ligament in his right wrist. He managed to finish the competition at 5-under-par, despite the injury. This marked his best finish in over a year, where he ended the tournament tied for 17th, 13 strokes behind 21-year-old winner Jordan Spieth, who made history with a first-place finish from start to finish, the first such achievement in 39 years.

Iker Casillas, a long-time goalkeeper for Real Madrid, has stated his intention to remain at the club despite speculation linking David de Gea of Manchester United to a move. Casillas, who has been at Real Madrid since the age of 16, hopes to fulfill his contract and compete for the starting position. He is currently focused on helping Real Madrid defend their Champions League title, with the semi-finals yet to be contested. The semi-finals also include arch-rivals Barcelona, Bayern Munich, and Juventus, making for exciting matches.

A video has surfaced of a failed S300 missile launch in Russia, where the rocket barely lifts off and plummets back down, followed by a loud explosion. This incident took place at an unknown military base. The footage may prove embarrassing for Russian President Vladimir Putin, given recent increases in the country's defense budget. This event is one of a series of such mishaps in Russia, with another incident causing the deaths of six ballistic missile technicians. The failed launch occurred in a region near Donetsk, Ukraine, with a second missile, the OTR-21 Tochka, successfully launched from the wreckage seconds later.

James Faulkner, the Australian World Cup-winning all-rounder, has signed with Lancashire as their overseas player for most of the summer. He will replace Peter Siddle, who will play for Lancashire in the first four LV= County Championship matches before joining the Australia squad. Notable for his performance in white-ball cricket, Faulkner is a versatile player with a strong record in first-class cricket, and Lancashire are excited to have him join their team after his Indian Premier League commitments.

Mary Kay Letourneau Fualaau, once a married teacher who engaged in an affair and sexual relationship with her 13-year-old student Vili Fualaau in 1996, will share details about her current happiness with Vili and their successful marriage in a forthcoming ABC interview. After serving more than seven years in prison for her actions, the couple, who now have two teenage daughters, wed in 2005 and have remained together. During the interview, Letourneau Fualau discusses her plans to return to teaching, her intentions to have her status as a registered sex offender lifted, and the challenges they've faced in their relationship, while Vili Fualau opens up about his struggles with alcoholism and depression.

Jamie Carragher, a former Liverpool player and current sports pundit, traveled to Girona, Spain, to watch his son James play in the Under 12s at the Mediterranean International Cup. The tournament, which showcases over 200 clubs from 36 countries, has previously featured football stars such as Lionel Messi, Cesc Fabregas, and Neymar. Carragher, who shared a photo from the opening ceremony on his Instagram, cheered his son's team, the Liverpool U12s, as they drew their first game 1-1 against CE Mercantil. Their subsequent matches are against CE Cristinenc and FE ATL Bisbalenc in Group E.

A Seattle-based filmmaker, Gabriel Ng, utilized a drone to capture breathtaking footage of Thailand's visual wonders, showcasing the country's stunning coastline, religious sites, and everyday life scenes. The six-minute video, primarily filmed on Ko Samui, presents breathtaking aerial views of peaceful rivers, waterfalls, mountains, fishing boats, and local landmarks like Wat Phra Yai (Big Buddha Temple). The video has garnered praise on YouTube, with viewers praising its cinematography quality, comparable to productions by the Discovery Channel. Gabriel, who has used drone-mounted cameras for various projects, including weddings and landscapes like Red Rock Canyon State Park and the Las Vegas Strip, has produced a compelling love letter to Thailand's beauty.

1. Despite a past conflict with Michael Vaughan, Peter Moores has expressed willingness to work with Vaughan if he becomes England's new director of cricket.

2. Moores has stated that he is uncertain about the necessity of another voice in the England dressing room, depending on who takes the director role and how the position is defined.

3. Moores has expressed sadness over the departure of Paul Downton, who played a significant role in bringing Moores back as England's coach, and has emphasized his focus on the upcoming Test series and his commitment to the emerging players in the team.

Nottingham Forest plans to renew its bid for £10million-rated Blackburn striker Jordan Rhodes this summer, having failed to sign him on loan in March. Rhodes, who has scored 70 goals in the last three seasons, has been a target for Forest, Derby, Norwich, and Middlesbrough by Blackburn, who have so far resisted all bids. Meanwhile, Blackburn manager Gary Bowyer anticipates interest in Rhodes' strike partner Rudy Gestede, who scored 19 goals this season, with Hull, Crystal Palace, West Brom, and Southampton reportedly considering a move.

A three-dog band consisting of a Husky named Sky, two Springer Spaniels named Sadie and Marshall, harmoniously performed a melodious ensemble by howling and barking in their North Carolina home. The performance began with Sadie barking and interacting with Sky, who then followed suit with a howl. Marshall added a growl-like baritone howl, culminating in a harmonious performance where the dogs pointed their noses to the sky. The impromptu concert ended when the owner instructed them to stop, catching the dogs off-guard.

The French Spiderman, Alain Robert, completed a daring climb of Dubai's twisting 75-storey Cayan Tower without the use of a safety harness or other equipment, using only sticky tape and chalk. The 52-year-old climber, who has survived falls during previous climbs worldwide, took an hour and a half for the ascent, with hundreds of spectators watching. Robert has previously been arrested, imprisoned, and banned from numerous locations for illegal ascents, but this marks his third climbing feat in Dubai.

An experimental cancer drug, AZDO5030, developed by Astra Zeneca and initially discarded due to poor cancer results, has shown potential in reversing the effects of Alzheimer's. The drug works by blocking a process that breaks nerve connections in the brain used for memory storage. Researchers at Yale University are now conducting human trials on Alzheimer's patients to assess its effectiveness. Dr James Pickett of the Alzheimer's Society expresses optimism about the drug's repurposing for Alzheimer's treatment, noting its potential cost and time effectiveness compared to developing new drugs.

1. Paul Bettany has been revealed to play the Vision, a long-awaited member of the Avengers team, in the upcoming movie "Avengers: Age of Ultron."
2. Marvel Studios also posted the first official image of Charlie Cox's Daredevil suit from the Netflix series "Daredevil," released a day before the series premiere.
3. In additon, director Bryan Singer announced that Ben Hardy would be playing the winged mutant character Angel in the next year's "X-Men: Apocalypse," and photos of Jamie Bell's Thing from the rebooted "Fantastic Four" movie were released, showing a similar appearance to the original character.

Kenny Bayless, a highly-regarded referee with experience overseeing both Floyd Mayweather and Manny Pacquiao's fights, has been selected to officiate their upcoming boxing match, considered the biggest and richest in history. However, former opponent of Mayweater, Oscar De La Hoya, claims the referee's appointment will serve as an advantage for Mayweather, suggesting that Bayless tends to break up fights too quickly when both fighters are clinched, potentially favoring Mayweather's defensive style.

1. Harry Kane's participation in the Under 21 European Championship is uncertain due to Tottenham scheduling a post-season friendly in Malaysia next month, with Kane included in the traveling squad for two exhibition games.
2. Spurs manager Mauricio Pochettino expressed concerns about Kane's potential burnout, and talks are ongoing with the FA over his possible involvement in the tournament. Despite wanting to play, Kane will miss the senior friendly against Ireland and the Euro 2016 qualifier against Slovenia.
3. Kane, who captained Tottenham in a 0-0 draw with Burnley, has previously scored 79 seconds into his England debut during a 4-0 win over Lithuania at Wembley last month, though he could not find a goal during the stalemate at Turf Moor on Sunday.

The California Department of Public Health declared an end to a measles outbreak that affected over 130 people since December, after 42 days without a new case. The outbreak began with visits to two Disney theme parks, and most of the patients were unvaccinated, accounting for 70% of those for whom vaccine status was known. The CDC lists 19 different measles strains discovered since 1990, with the disease being a highly contagious respiratory illness causing fever, reddened eyes, runny nose, cough, and rash, potentially leading to severe complications like pneumonia and encephalitis, spread through coughing or sneezing, and remaining in the air and on surfaces for up to two hours.

A family-of-six, comprising two adults and four children, has been sought by the Argentine police for reckless driving after they were spotted cramming onto a single motorbike without helmets in San Miguel de Tucuman, riding through the city without helmets. This incident follows a similar instance involving a family of seven riding on the same motorbike in Junin, Argentina. The surprising and dangerous act sparked criticism on social media, with users expressing concern for the children's safety. Authorities have urged anyone recognizing the family to come forward, strongly condemning their irresponsible behavior.

Andrea McVeigh, a 44-year-old social media manager, was seriously injured after being knocked down by a cyclist riding on the pavement in Bermondsey, south London. The cyclist fled the scene, but CCTV footage of the incident has been released, and the police are seeking to identify the cyclist. McVeigh suffered significant facial injuries, including two three-inch gashes to her forehead, and is currently off work recovering from her injuries.

In the Washburn Street Cemetery in Scranton, Pennsylvania, the headstone of Hillary Clinton's father, Hugh Rodham, was found tipped over on Monday, just two days after Clinton announced her run for the White House. Local resident Paul McGloin, who tends to Rodham's grave, found the headstone in this state and is not sure if it was a case of vandalism or weather-related damage. Police are investigating the incident and suspect vandalism as the most likely cause, with funeral director Neil Regan sharing similar sentiments. Local resident McGloin questions if this occurrence was a coincidence, given its timing with Clinton's presidential announcement.

A California woman, Beatriz Paez, claims a U.S. Marshal broke her phone and interrupted her recording of a police incident in South Gate, California. Paez has filed a complaint and is considering a lawsuit. The police department does not have authority over U.S. Marshals, complicating Paez's official complaint. U.S. Representative Janice Hahn wants a federal investigation into the Marshall's actions, arguing they were illegal as Paez was not hindering an investigation or arrest.

Max, a husky-corgi hybrid, stands at 18.5 inches tall and was abandoned in Essex, sought refuge at the Dogs Trust. Despite his small stature, Max is a fully-grown canine. His unique origin stems from a hypothetical encounter between one of Queen's corgis and Sir Ranulph Fiennes' Siberian husky. Due to his appearance in shows like Game of Thrones, huskies like Max have gained popularity, but many new owners find it challenging to care for their specific needs, often leading to abandonment.

Chilean pickpockets are the most successful thieves in central London, using strategies such as following wealthy shoppers and posing as families or business groups to blend in. They are known for their intelligence-led approach, often targeting wealthy tourists. Police are frequently monitoring these groups with the assistance of CCTV to drive down pickpocket crimes, especially in busy shopping areas like Oxford Street. A significant number of pickpockets arrested in the region are reportedly from Romania, Bulgaria, and Algeria, with Chileans comprising around 5% of the total, according to DC Darren Bond.

A driver in his 20s survived a severe car accident where his vehicle flipped over and he was trapped. Firefighters took 25 minutes to free him, discovering his navy blue jeans were firmly stuck under the car. The man sustained head, chest, and suspected leg fractures but remained conscious. Emergency services express gratitude for his survival given the crash's severity.

A 40-tonne pile of industrial waste, including materials from the carpet and veterinary industries, has been illegally dumped at the side of a road in Walsham-le-Willows, Suffolk. The fly-tipping incident, deemed the worst in almost 30 years by a rural crime officer, is believed to have been committed using three tractors and trailers. Local authorities and environmental agencies are now working together to clear the waste and address the issue of fly-tipping, with increased efforts led by the police, National Farmers' Union, and Country Land and Business Association.

A man at Toronto's Pearson International Airport was Tasered after he refused to comply with security protocol, attempted to enter a restricted area, and resisted police orders not to board a Turkish Airlines flight. The incident was caught on video, showing the man visibly shaking after the Tasering before being brought to the ground. He was later handcuffed and taken to a hospital under Canada's Mental Health Act, but it remains unclear whether criminal charges will be brought against him.

1. A government jet carrying Serbia's President Tomislav Nikolic to Italy last week was forced to return to Belgrade due to a co-pilot spilling coffee on the instrument board during a turbulent flight, causing the plane to tumble.
2. The incident caused advisers to be "thrown around the cabin" and "threatened another malfunction" on the ageing aircraft, forcing the president to cancel his official visit to meet Pope Francis in the Vatican.
3. An investigation found that the co-pilot accidentally activated the emergency slat button while wiping the coffee off the instrument board, causing the autopilot to turn off, the plane to lose altitude, and one engine to stop working temporarily. The co-pilot's license was subsequently suspended.

In South Africa, over 300 suspects have been arrested for deadly attacks on foreigners that forced thousands to flee, with the government strongly condemning the violence. The attacks led to the death of five people, including a 14-year-old boy, and sparked heavy police response to prevent further violence. The government and local charities urged citizens to remember the country's history of African support during Apartheid and called for an end to the xenophobic attacks, as tens of thousands sought shelter. Notably, President Jacob Zuma visited displaced foreign nationals in Chatsworth to express his support, and charity Gift of the Givers offered shelter to immigrants in Johannesburg. The city has a history of anti-immigrant tensions, with deadly attacks in 2008 primarily targeting Zimbabweans fleeing repression and economic hardship.

In Revelstoke, Canada, photographer Zach Birnie was filming the scenic mountainside when an unexpected avalanche occurred while he was skiing off-piste. The skier manages to survive the incident but sustains minor injuries and is submerged beneath the snow for a period of time. Cornelia Accola from the WSL Institute for Snow and Avalanche Research SLF theorizes the fresh snow and steep terrain might have caused the avalanche and advises that if one finds themselves in a similar situation, they should try to escape the avalanche area, let go of their ski poles, open their bindings, pull their knees towards their chest, and hold their arms in front of their face.

On the hottest day of the year, two men robbed an Esso petrol station in Surrey by forcing their way into the manager's office in search of cash. They were caught on CCTV, bare-chested, during the robbery. The police have released these images and are appealing for public help in identifying them. A third suspect, also in his 20s, was arrested and later released on police bail while the investigation continues.

1. The Lada Niva 4x4 is priced at £13,395 on the road, potentially experiencing a sales boom due to the Land Rover Defender's discontinuation. Known for its robust nature and chunky looks, the Niva has garnered fans worldwide.

2. The Niva is a no-frills off-road vehicle, offering a functional yet easy-to-clean plastic interior, particularly practical for muddy terrains. However, it has been reported that Russian President Vladimir Putin fitted a German engine to his Lada Niva in 2009.

3. While the Niva is an affordable and rugged 4x4 option, it does lack the luxuries often associated with more expensive vehicles such as Land Rovers. Its simplicity offers a degree of practicality, however, with the added advantage of an easy-to-clean interior.

A lawsuit accuses the AIDS Healthcare Foundation, the nation's largest supplier of HIV/AIDS medical care, of a $20 million dollar scam involving kickbacks for patient referrals to boost funding from federal health programs. This alleged practice was key to the company's business model. The suit was filed by three former managers who were later fired after reporting the issue, which the foundation denies, stating they are not guilty of wrongdoing. The lawsuit has been supported by the federal government and the state of Florida, who declined to intervene.

A bearded dragon named Liz, owned by Shannen Hussein, has demonstrated an ability to respond to questions about being hungry, as seen in a video taken at mealtime. Liz nods her head in agreement when asked if she is hungry. She is rewarded with a superworm treat, which she enjoys. Other notable pets owned by Shannen include a pet lamb named Winter, who has gained internet fame, and other animals such as cats, birds, a snake, and ducklings that live on her hobby farm and are featured on her popular social media channels.

Travis Hatfield, a 21-year-old country singer from West Virginia, gained viral fame after posting a video of him singing a George Jones hit to his 47-year-old uncle, Jamie Joe Cline, who has Down syndrome. The heartwarming video, which has over 410,000 views, portrays the two singing together weekly, with Travis hoping to secure a record deal in Nashville and potentially audition for The Voice 2016. The duo's bond is strong, with Travis considering Jamie his inspiration and sometimes musical partner.

High-wire performer Nik Wallenda plans to walk untethered on top of the 400-foot Orlando Eye observation wheel in Orlando, Florida, on April 29. This feat will take place while the wheel is in motion, making it a challenging and unique performance. Known for his death-defying stunts, Wallenda has previously walked across the Grand Canyon, Niagara Falls, and performed a blindfolded walk between two Chicago skyscrapers.

Bayern Munich's central defender Medhi Benatia could miss both legs of the Champions League quarter-final against Porto due to a muscle injury sustained in the German Cup last eight against Bayer Leverkusen. The defender is expected to be out for between two to four weeks, joining a list of injured players that includes Bastian Schweinsteiger, David Alaba, Javi Martinez, and reserve keeper Tom Starke. Bayern manager Pep Guardiola has a depleted squad as he prepares for domestic and European competition, with Franck Ribery and Thiago Alcantara recently returning from injuries. Despite the injuries and tough schedule, Bayern is still in the running for three titles, leading the Bundesliga by 10 points.

Bayern Munich, under coach Pep Guardiola, defeated Porto 6-1 in the Champions League quarter-finals, increasing their goal total for the season to 115. This dominating performance indicates Bayern's strong pursuit of a third consecutive title, the German Cup, and potentially additional Champions League matches. Notable goal scorers this season include Robert Lewandowski, Thiago Alcantara, Sebastian Rode, Mario Götze, Thomas Müller, Arjen Robben, Jerome Boateng, Holger Badstuber, and Sebastian Rode, with Lewandowski leading the pack. The team's current goal-scoring rate suggests a potential season total of 141 goals.

Fernando Torres, a former player of Atletico Madrid, has credited manager Diego Simeone as the key to the team's success, which includes six consecutive victories over Real Madrid. Simeone's leadership has allowed Atletico to exceed expectations and compete with top European teams, while also emphasizing the importance of playing at their limit due to limited resources compared to teams like Real Madrid, Barcelona, Bayern Munich, and Chelsea. Torres and several other Atletico players, including Cristian Ansaldi, Jesus Gamez, Gabi, and Mario Suarez, are one booking away from suspension for the upcoming Champions League quarter-final against Real Madrid.

A small aircraft carrying two passengers went missing and was later found crashed near Loch Etive, about 30 miles east of Oban in western Scotland. After the plane lost radar contact near Beinn Nan Lus, police, lifeboats, and helicopters were scrambled to aid in the search. Enquiries are ongoing to determine the exact circumstances of the crash, and the families of the victims are being supported by Police Scotland.

A bus collided with a Boeing 777 jet from Uzbekistan Airways at Tashkent airport, causing significant damage to the plane's engine. The incident resulted in delays for many passengers, though it's unclear if anyone was injured. This type of incident, including previous collisions involving Ryanair and British Airways planes, is becoming more common in airport tarmacs.

An off-duty Secret Service agent, identified as Arthur Baldwin, was arrested in the early hours of Friday in Washington D.C., charged with attempted burglary and destruction of property. The incident occurred on the 3200 block of D Street SE. Baldwin, who works in the Foreign Missions Branch of the service, has been placed on leave. This arrest follows a previous allegation of misconduct against a high-ranking supervisor, also being investigated by the Homeland Security Department's inspector general. Both incidents have raised concerns about the agency's oversight and can be seen as additional black eyes for the Secret Service, responsible for protecting the president and his family.

Israel is developing a new, high-tech system to accurately detect tunneling activity along its border with Gaza, with the potential to drastically reduce false alarms. The system, estimated to cost around £2.3million ($3.5m) per mile to install, aims to mitigate the threat posed by cross-border tunnels, a concern reiterated by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in 2014. The new system has successfully passed initial tests, with further results expected in the coming months.

A primary school headteacher has implemented a water-only policy during school hours to promote long-term health among students. Some parents, however, feel this rule is excessive, arguing that many children dislike water and find it difficult to stay hydrated without alternative drink options. This decision has sparked controversy among parents who believe it infringes on their right to choose their child's drinks. The school defending its decision, citing health benefits. Similar controversies over drink policies have occurred in other schools.

Paul Smith has secured a highly challenging fight against Andre Ward on June 20, and although it won't involve Ward's WBA super-middleweight world title, it presents a significant opportunity for Smith, who has previously failed in attacks on Arthur Abraham's WBO belt. Smith had previously outclassed Carl Froch and expressed excitement about testing himself against top-level fighter Ward, who has not fought since November 2013. Ward, despite his extended inactivity, is confident in his ability to defeat Smith.

1. German Chancellor Angela Merkel and her husband Joachim Sauer are spending their annual Easter holiday on the Italian island of Ischia, traditionally at the luxurious Miramare Spa Hotel, due to a cooler-than-usual climate.
2. To maintain her fitness regime, Merkel has reportedly hired a private Pilates instructor and is choosing vegetarian meals during her stay. The Miramare Spa Hotel offers a range of amenities, including thermal baths, a spa center, and private beach.
3. Merkel's husband, professor of theoretical chemistry Joachim Sauer, is typically not seen in public with her and avoids media attention, a preference that continued as he skipped her inauguration in 2005.

Ander Herrera, a Spanish midfielder playing for Manchester United, has an unusual shooting habit – he often scores goals while apparently keeping his eyes shut. His most recent brace against Aston Villa, as well as several earlier goals, were scored without looking at the ball or the goal. Former Athletic Bilbao player Herrera, who joined United for £29million due to his vision and creativity in midfield, has been praised by Louis van Gaal for his shooting technique.

A 23-month-old girl sadly passed away in North Las Vegas after being unintentionally hit by her father's pickup truck in the driveway. The family was unaware that the toddler had left the house and reached the driveway. Officials have termed the incident an accident and no charges will be filed. The identities of the family members involved have not been disclosed to the public.

The University of Connecticut baseball team has welcomed a new member, 5-year-old Grayson Hand who is battling leukemia, as part of a program by Team IMPACT. Grayson will have his own locker with the team and can attend as many games and practices as he likes. His sister, Sophie, 7, was also named an honorary cheerleader. The Hands view this partnership as a tangible symbol of the emotional support they've received during their battle with cancer.

London Midland has committed to providing CCTV footage of a passenger who defecated in a train carriage during a service between Lichfield Trent Valley and Longbridge. The incident caused severe delays and disrupted the Cross City line. Passenger Christopher Talbot discovered the feces in a newspaper on the train on Thursday morning and reported it to platform staff. London Midland has promised to pass the CCTV footage to police for investigation. The service resumed at about 9:30am following the cleaning of the carriage. This is not the first incident of its kind; a British Airways flight was previously aborted due to a foul smell from an overflowing toilet last month.

James Rodriguez, the Real Madrid midfielder, has been praised by Spanish newspaper Marca for his impressive form and significant impact since joining from Monaco last summer. The Colombian star, dubbed 'the jewel in Real Madrid's crown', has contributed 13 goals and 12 assists, with the team winning 80% of games when he's on the field compared to 58% when he's not. Marca credits him for living up to his £60million price-tag. Meanwhile, AS focuses on Real's appeal against Cristiano Ronaldo's yellow card for diving in a match against Rayo Vallecano, and Italy's La Gazzetta dello Sport reports Roberto Mancini's plans for revamping Inter Milan's squad, with players like Yaya Toure, Filipe Luis, and Paulo Dybala potential targets. Tuttosport, on the other hand, claims that Alvaro Morata, a Juventus striker, is not interested in a return to Real Madrid.

A Florida man, identified as Kenneth Crowder, claimed to be God and was high on the designer drug Flakka, stronger than crystal meth. On Friday, he was seen running naked through a neighborhood and committing an undisclosed act on a tree. When police arrived, they used a Taser twice on him, but he violently resisted. He was later arrested and charged with battery on a law-enforcement officer, resisting with violence, and assault with a deadly weapon on a law-enforcement officer. Flakka, a dangerous drug usually made from alpha-PVP, causes euphoria, hallucinations, and sometimes psychosis or apparent superhuman strength. Its use has significantly increased in Florida, with more than 670 occurrences in 2014.

A Russian Premier League match between Arsenal Tula and Torpedo Moscow was suspended for seven minutes due to rival fan violence during the 31st minute, as Torpedo fans broke down barriers, broke seats, and threw them at law enforcement officers and stewards. The Torpedo fans caused chaos, with fights breaking out on the running track, and the match was briefly halted before resuming with Torpedo winning 3-1. The Russian Football Premier League executive director, Sergei Cheban, warned of severe punishment for Torpedo, as it has a history of fan violence and racism, previously causing trouble on multiple occasions and being sanctioned three times this season.

High school girls in China receive military-style dagger training from a former special forces soldier, Inspector Tan, at the 27th March Huizhou Integrated High School. The training, which includes shouts of "kill, stab, slash and jab," employs plastic knives with retractable blades, aiming for self-defense skills without endangering students. The instruction is part of a school-wide plan to provide self-defense training for every female student, with the goal of enabling them to use everyday items like chopsticks to defend themselves. The five-day training session has been well received by the students, who are learning the latest self-defense techniques.

AP McCoy, the champion jockey who has held the title every year since 1997, plans to retire immediately if his mount, Shutthefrontdoor, wins the £1 million Crabbie’s Grand National on Saturday. With an avalanche of emotional support for this race known for its unpredictability, McCoy hopes to end his record-breaking career with a victory on Shutthefrontdoor. He has previously won the Grand National in 2010 on Don’t Push It and expressed his dream of finishing the race high in his irons celebrating.

John Isner, a 6-foot-10 American tennis player, reached the semifinals of the Miami Open by defeating Kei Nishikori 6-4, 6-3, marking the first time an American man has achieved this in Miami since 2011. Isner, known for his powerful serve, faced no break chances throughout the tournament and never faced serious trouble during the match. In the other semifinal, Andy Murray will play Tomas Berdych, where Murray may find himself facing animosity as Berdych's fitness coach and former assistant coach of Murray were once close friends who had a contentious match at this year's Australian Open. Murray's wife, Kim Sears, was reported to have expressed displeasure towards Berdych during their Australian Open encounter.

In the first leg of the Champions League quarter-final, Bayern Munich suffered a 3-1 defeat by Porto, with Franz Beckenbauer criticizing defender Dante's performance, calling it reminiscent of someone wearing "ski boots." Beckenbauer, a former player and current brand ambassador for the club, made these remarks during a press event in New York as part of Bayern's media agreement with MSN. He also characterized the entire team's performance as if they had taken "sleeping pills," and expressed concern about their chances of advancing to the semi-finals, given their recent form.

A 21-year-old man named Arnold Quintero from San Antonio, Texas, has been arrested for allegedly imprisoning, beating, sexually assaulting, and burning a 13-year-old girl. He faces multiple charges, including aggravated sexual assault of a child and sex performed by a child under 14. The girl was held in a 'trap' house in January and February, during which she was physically and sexually abused. She identified Quintero in a photo lineup, and he is currently in jail with several charges remaining. The investigation was conducted by the Bexar County Sheriff’s Office.

In Week 12 of the Betway Premier League, Michael van Gerwen (World No 1) had a mixed night, winning 7-0 against James Wade and booking a spot in the play-offs, but losing 7-5 to Gary Anderson in the finale. Gary Anderson, too, had a topsy-turvy night, losing 7-1 to Stephen Bunting in the opener but clinching a thrilling 7-5 win over Van Gerwen in the finale, averaging 105.94. Other notable matches included Raymond van Barneveld defeating Dave Chisnall 7-5 and Phil Taylor drawing 6-6 with Adrian Lewis.

Jay Rutland, a training consultant and husband to billionaire heiress Tamara Ecclestone, earned £65 a week from his firm, Brigante Business Developments, in the year of 2014, leaving the company with net assets of £3,378. The firm, which provides management consultancy activities, saw a significant decrease from the prior year's net assets of £18,131. Rutland, who was previously a stockbroker, has had a controversial career, including a ban from trading in 2012 due to market abuse and a mugging in 2013. Despite these financial and personal setbacks, the couple, who married in 2013, live in a £45million house in London and enjoy a lavish lifestyle, with expensive cars and extravagant parties for their daughter Sophia.

A leukaemia patient named Jia Binhui, aged 25 and originally from a family of poor farm workers, has resorted to an unconventional treatment due to financial constraints, as hospital treatments have depleted his savings. He builds a homemade contraption in his garden in Yunlong County, Yunnan Province, where he lies above a fire, hoping the temperatures above 42 degrees Celsius will kill his cancerous cells. Despite the unorthodox nature of his treatment, Jia remains hopeful and determined, having recently married his long-term girlfriend, Liu Yuan.

Queens Park Rangers are hoping to boost their relegation fight by bringing Leroy Fer back from a knee injury as soon as possible, with the Dutch midfielder aiming to return to the squad for the home London derby against West Ham. However, manager Chris Ramsey is aware that rushing Fer back could risk another injury due to his recent struggles with form and fitness since joining from Norwich in the summer. Additionally, QPR have a number of players returning from injury, including Richard Dunne and Yun Suk-Young, while Rio Ferdinand remains unavailable.

1. Team Sky riders Sir Bradley Wiggins and Geraint Thomas managed to avoid a major crash in the final kilometre of Scheldeprijs race, but teammate Elia Viviani was involved and went to the hospital for x-rays after hitting the barriers and crashing.
2. Elia Viviani sustained injuries to his arm and ribs, with the remainder of Team Sky's riders escaping involvement in the incident.
3. The crash occurred near the expected sprint finish in the cobbled classic, with Katusha's Alexander Kristoff ultimately claiming victory, as only 14 riders contested the sprint finish following the accident.

Aston Villa players received messages of encouragement from fans, displayed in their dressing room before the FA Cup semi-final against Liverpool. Jack Grealish, a 19-year-old player, thanked supporters on Twitter, encouraging the team to find the 'end of the rainbow' and prove they're the pride of the Midlands. Coach Tim Sherwood included Grealish in the starting line-up after his impressive performances, and other players like Brad Guzan also shared supportive messages prior to the match.

A 12-year-old named Hanghang in China was severely injured when his old phone exploded while charging, exposing part of his jawbone and embedding fragments in his arms and legs. He had used the phone as an alarm and played with it before it became hot and blew up. Experts speculate that improper charging might be the most common cause of such explosions, and advise against using the phone during charging, not overcharging, and replacing swollen batteries. Hanghang is currently hospitalized and expected to undergo several surgeries.

Mike Rowe, in an episode of "Somebody's Gotta Do It," met Chad Pregracke, the founder of Living Lands & Waters, a nonprofit that aims to clean U.S. rivers. Pregracke, who founded the organization at 23, has collected over 8.4 million pounds of trash with the help of thousands of volunteers, and won the 2013 CNN Hero of the Year Award. Pregracke also showed Rowe his living and working barge, made from a recycled strip club, and hopes to remove an additional 500,000 pounds of trash in 2015, encouraging viewers to get involved at LivingLandsAndWaters.org/Get-Involved/.

The drone-captured footage showcases the spooky, abandoned ghost town of Balestrino, a Tuscan settlement dating back to the 11th century, with a castle on the hill and depreciated buildings. The town, located 40 miles southeast of Genoa, was mostly abandoned due to seismic instability caused by earthquakes, with a destructive one in 1887 measuring 6.7 on the Richter scale. The town is well-known as the most famous abandoned location in Italy and is rumored to be haunted.

The article discusses an event in Anaheim, California where director J.J. Abrams and the cast of "Star Wars: Episode VII - The Force Awakens" screened the film's trailer, delighting the audience. Highlights of the event include the return of Han Solo and Chewbacca, the new planet setting of Jakku, hints of the involvement of Leia, Luke, and other characters, less CGI use in the film, and the physical presence of the new droid BB-8. Henry Hanks, CNN's reporter present at the event, shares five key takeaways, including the reappearance of Han Solo, the location of the initial action on the planet Jakku, hints of Leia and Luke's involvement, the reduced use of CGI, and the physical nature of the new droid BB-8.

Rob Ford, the former Toronto Mayor, has announced he will undergo a serious surgery on May 11 to remove a cancerous tumor from his abdomen. The surgery, which will be performed by four surgeons, is expected to last eight to ten hours and he may need to stay in the hospital for 10 to 14 days. Ford was diagnosed with malignant liposarcoma last year and underwent chemotherapy and radiation treatments, which have significantly shrunk the tumor. He expressed hope to return to work as a councilor in September.

The University of Cape Town has removed a statue of British colonialist Cecil Rhodes, a decision driven by student protests which claimed the statue represented racism. The statue's removal came after weeks of campaigns, such as #RhodesMustFall, that argued Rhodes' legacy did not align with contemporary values. However, some contend the removal is an erasure of history, as seen in protests over the removal of similar statues in Pretoria. The students, elated by the statue's removal, have marked the occasion with a celebratory march, declaring "we're not done yet."

Michael Phelps, the 18-time Olympic gold-medalist, successfully returned to competitive swimming after a six-month ban due to a drink-driving conviction, winning the 100 meters butterfly race at the Arena Pro Swim Series in Arizona. With a time of 52.38 seconds, Phelps edged out Ryan Lochte. Despite missing this summer's World Championships in Kazan, Russia, following talks with USA Swimming, Phelps aims to compete in his fifth Olympics in 2016 at Rio de Janeiro.

A woman in Crown Heights, New York hung herself from a third-floor fire escape early Sunday morning. Her body was discovered at around 8:20 am and remained there for over an hour. Several witnesses were traumatized, with one initially believing it was a Halloween prank. The woman had known mental health issues. Her identity has not been released, pending notification of her family.

1. Lyon and Saint-Etienne played a stirring derby match on Sunday, with Lyon securing a 2-2 draw, led by Clinton N'Jie's goal and a late equalizer from Christophe Jallet.

2. In a separate game, Lille cemented their position as a serious contender for a top-four spot in Ligue 1, winning 2-0 against Bordeaux, with goals from Nolan Roux and Adama Traore, leaving them just four points behind Bordeaux.

3. In another clash, Hilton's early header was enough to give Montpellier a 1-0 victory over Caen, moving them up to seventh place in the standings, while Caen fell to 13th after a run of poor results.

Arsene Wenger was surprised by the significant contributions of Hector Bellerin and Francis Coquelin in Arsenal's late push for the Premier League title, as he initially did not foresee them as key players. Bellerin, who was on loan at Watford last year, scored a crucial goal against Liverpool and showcased impressive defensive skills against Raheem Sterling. Coquelin was previously sent on loan to Charlton, but has since become a vital player for Arsenal. Despite Bellerin being booked for a slide tackle on Sterling, Wenger praised his maturity and overall performance.

"The Rocky Horror Picture Show," the iconic 1975 cult classic musical, is being remade for television by Fox. The two-hour special, tentatively titled "The Rocky Horror Picture Show Event," will be directed, executive-produced, and choreographed by Kenneth Ortega, and is casting-contingent. It will be produced by Fox 21 Television Studios and The Jackal Group, with Gail Berman and Lou Adler, producers of the original film, serving as executive producers. The project is timed to celebrate the film's 40th anniversary, with plans to air the special sometime in the future.
