This isn't the first attempt to adapt the film for television, as Fox had plans for an adaptation in 2002 that ultimately did not come to fruition. Fox also has a live musical production of "Grease" scheduled to air in January 2016, and NBC is preparing to air a live version of "The Wiz" later this year.

AS Roma has been ordered to close part of their stadium for an upcoming home game due to an offensive banner displayed during a recent match against Napoli, which offensively referred to the mother of a Napoli fan who was killed in violent clashes last year. The banner caused outrage as it was deemed provocative and disrespectful. Roma's next game against Atalanta on April 19 will see part of the Stadio Olimpico Stadium closed. The banners aimed at Antonella Leardi, the mother of the deceased Ciro Esposito, were met with condemnation by Roma's club president James Pallotta, who expressed the club's deep regret over such incidents. Leardi, who has been advocating against football violence, expressed her pain over the offensive words.

Ellen White, former Arsenal player, experienced a memorable night in the Women's Super League as she scored a stunning free-kick against her old club, Notts County. The goal came from a perfectly executed set-piece, which was nearly disrupted by a mistake from Laura Bassett and Alex Greenwood. However, the game ended in a 1-1 draw, with White's former team salvaging a point after Chioma Ubogagu scored her debut goal. White also missed a penalty that could have extended Notts County's lead.

1. Arsene Wenger acknowledges discussions to sign Eden Hazard from Lille in 2012, but did not proceed due to financial limitations, as Chelsea eventually signed him for £32 million.
2. Eden Hazard has had an outstanding season for Chelsea, leading to speculation about the Player of the Season award, which Wenger predicts will be a close contest between Hazard and Arsenal's Alexis Sanchez.
3. Wenger commends Hazard for his improved final ball, maturity on the pitch, and ability to turn games, attributing him a high level of quality, but believes Alexis Sanchez's relative inexperience in the Premier League may affect the Player of the Season vote.

Stephen Akers-Belcher was dismissed from his care manager role with Newcastle City Council for gross misconduct, after he was found to have taken unauthorized leave and allegedly attended a warship event, instead of the funeral he claimed to attend. Akers-Belcher had made whistleblowing allegations about the authority's protection of vulnerable adults, but the council firmly denied that his dismissal was related to those allegations. Akers-Belcher claimed his visit to the Hartlepool-related HMS Warrior in Portsmouth was for learning about regeneration and tourism promotion for Hartlepool, but the council has not commented further on the matter.

A highly respected Australian doctor named John Parker, who had been working at an Ebola treatment center in Sierra Leone since November, was placed in isolation at Westmead Hospital in Sydney after experiencing flu-like symptoms. Tests taken at the hospital came back negative for Ebola, as confirmed by NSW Health. The aid organization Aspen Medical, which employs Dr. Parker, stated that he followed protocol by notifying authorities as a precaution.

A nine-year-old British football player named Frankie Franz has successfully replicated Barcelona's Martin Montoya's viral trick shot, scoring a 27-yard goal into a basketball hoop twice. Inspired by Montoya's video at Barcelona's Ciutat Esportiva, Frankie, who plays for Dagenham and Redbridge Football Club, moved the basketball hoop into the center of his garden goal before executing the shot, sending the ball straight through the net on the first try. Delighted by the achievement, Frankie plans to continue working on his amazing skill set with dreams of playing for either Real Madrid or Barcelona in the future.

The Wisden–MCC Cricket Photograph of the Year 2014 showcases a wide array of cricket images globally, capturing both professional games and enthusiastic amateurs. The winning photograph, by Matthew Lewis, is of Dwayne Bravo taking a stunning catch for the West Indies in the ICC World Twenty20 against Australia. Other notable images range from children playing on a rubbish tip in Bangladesh to players attempting a catch in Kent, England.

A New Jersey judge has ruled that a mother did not abuse her parental discretion by taking her 11-year-old daughter to a Pink concert in 2013, despite the father's protests. The father, who is the girl's ex-husband, claimed the performances were too sexually suggestive. However, the judge found that Pink's music, while sometimes suggestive, is not necessarily inappropriate for preteens. The judge also noted that the mother's decision was reasonable, as she took the girl's wishes into account and deemed the show age-appropriate after watching clips on YouTube.

1. Salcombe in Devon, previously known as one of the UK's most expensive seaside resorts, has recently surpassed London in terms of average property cost, with a staggering £671,759.

2. The average cost of a waterfront property in Salcombe reaches over £2 million, eclipsing even some of London's prestigious neighborhoods such as Notting Hill, Regent's Park, and Hampstead Heath.

3. Despite the steep property prices, the Salcombe Harbour Hotel offers accommodations starting from £425 for those interested in experiencing the affluent coastal town this summer season. Known as the "Chelsea-on-Sea," Salcombe boasts its picturesque waterfront, thriving yachting culture, fresh seafood, and beautiful beaches.

1. Celtic football club has criticized the Scotland Football Association (SFA) for setting high ticket prices for their Scottish Cup semi-final against Inverness Caledonian Thistle at Hampden this month.
2. Celtic argues that the pricing, with £23 for the North and South stands, is too high for their supporters, particularly since a large number will be required to pay these prices due to the team's fanbase.
3. In response, the SFA stated that all four participating clubs were consulted on ticket pricing, which has been unchanged for the past four years, and that revenues from the semi-final gate, broadcast, and advertising are aggregated and evenly distributed among the teams, with a 10-percent levy.

A 16-year-old student, Rebecca Rice, was allowed to bring her pet Labrador, Holly, into her GCSE French oral exam at Bodmin College in Cornwall to alleviate her severe nervousness. This decision was made after discussing potential calming strategies with teacher Lorette Esteve, who recognized Holly as the only thing that comforted Rebecca. Following the exam, Rebecca confirmed that having Holly present greatly reduced her nerves. The school has previously implemented stress-reducing measures like bringing desired items or having a friend in the room during exams.

Anders Lindegaard, a Manchester United goalkeeper, shared a day off with his wife Misse Beqiri amidst the English weather. They married last year in a romantic beach wedding in Mauritius and have a son together. Beqiri, a Swedish model of Albanian descent, often posts modelling photos on her Instagram. Lindegaard's football career at United has been limited due to competition from David de Gea and Victor Valdes, with him currently as the third-choice goalkeeper. Despite this, he has had success off the pitch.

Manchester United goalkeepers David de Gea and Victor Valdes took a break from football to visit a theme park, wearing sunglasses and enjoying a day off following a recent impressive win against Manchester City. Despite a rollercoaster season, United have emerged as rivals for second place in the Premier League after a successful run of six wins in a row. However, the future of both De Gea and Valdes remains uncertain, with Valdes' opportunities limited since joining on a free transfer.

A piano teacher, John Goodwin, awaiting trial for six counts of aggravated sexual assault against an underage student, shot himself outside a New Hampshire courthouse while jurors were deliberating. The former student testified he did not come forward until 2013 due to embarrassment. Goodwin was airlifted to a hospital with life-threatening injuries, but his current health status is not immediately known. The trial proceedings continue as the New Hampshire Attorney General's Office investigates the incident.

Amazon removed a controversial mobile game, titled "Rescue the Anorexia Girl," after it received numerous complaints for encouraging players to feed a cartoon character battling anorexia by throwing food at her. The game's design, which portrays anorexia as a villain that needs to be defeated, was criticized for reinforcing harmful stereotypes and stigmatizing those suffering from mental illnesses, with some pointedly comparing it to mocking individuals with cystic fibrosis. Eating disorders are known to have the highest mortality rate among mental illnesses, and experts argued that the game could discourage individuals from seeking help.

Scientists are working on a project called the Green Brain Project, aimed at digitally recreating the cognitive abilities of honeybees to power drones. The ultimate goal is to create a robot that thinks, senses, and acts like the insect. So far, scientists have successfully replicated the portion of the honeybee's brain responsible for sight. The artificial brain is being tested on three quadcopters and one ground robot, with initial tests showing promising results. The project is ongoing, with plans to further develop navigation, cognitive functions, and the integration of chemosensors.

A newly-wed Air Malta crew, comprising a pilot and a cabin crew member, arranged a romantic flight over the Mediterranean to celebrate their wedding. The Airbus A319 flew heart-shaped patterns and a sightseeing tour, with the wedding party onboard. The special flight caused curiosity among aviation enthusiasts, who speculated it was a training exercise or a publicity stunt; however, Air Malta confirmed it was a romantic gesture by the newly-weds for their family and friends.

A five-year-old giraffe named Melvin was gored to death by an eland antelope at Kristiansand zoo in Norway. Witnesses, including 30 children, saw the unprovoked attack, which occurred when Melvin got his head stuck in the fence. Veterinary efforts to save Melvin, who was a popular attraction at the zoo, were unsuccessful. The cause of the attack remains unknown.

A restaurant in Belgium, Rubens eaterie, has been criticized for charging a mother 36p to heat up her baby's feeding bottle. The incident went viral after the mother, Gitte Denteneer, shared a photo of the bill on Twitter, sparking outrage. The restaurant chain later stated that this service is typically free, but it could be charged if customers are explicitly informed.

1. North Korea accused Mexico of illegally detaining one of its cargo ships, the Mu Du Bong, which ran aground off the coast of Mexico in July, claiming the Mexican government is violating the crew members' human rights by keeping them from their families.

2. Mexico defended its actions, stating that the company that owns the ship, North Korea's Ocean Maritime Management company, has previously skirted United Nations sanctions, making the detainment a valid move based on international obligations.

3. The incident echoes an earlier one in 2013 when Panama detained another North Korean ship, the Chong Chon Gang, finding it was carrying undeclared weaponry from Cuba. In that case, Panama eventually released the ship after North Korea agreed to pay a fine.

David Cameron is planning to offer an additional 600,000 childcare spaces for families a year to encourage employment, addressing the high costs of nurseries and childminders as a significant employment barrier. This initiative will be funded by reducing tax relief on pension contributions for those earning more than £150,000 per year. Cameron aims to double the existing 15 hours of free childcare a week for three- and four-year-olds, offering 30 hours of free childcare for this age group, helping families save around £5,000 annually and work an extra 78 days a year without childcare costs by 2017. The Conservative Party's emphasis is on promoting employment and reducing poverty through the principle of "something for something, not something for nothing."

Manchester City's young team secured a place in the Youth Cup final against Chelsea, winning 5-1 on aggregate after late goals from Isaac Buckley and Brandon Barker against Leicester City. Despite a penalty goal from Layton Ndukwu, Leicester could not overcome the three-goal deficit from the first leg. The first leg of the final is scheduled for April 20 at the City Football Academy Stadium.

Russian President Vladimir Putin dismissed Western sanctions against his country as an attempt to stymie Russian development, not just a response to the annexation of Crimea or the conflict in Ukraine's east. He also defended the sale of a sophisticated air defense system to Iran, calling it a defensive measure, and claimed Iran poses no threat to Israel. The annual question-and-answer session between Putin and Russians, which often stretches for hours, has been criticized as an imitation of democracy, with few opportunities for truly critical questions to be heard. In the past, notable figures like Edward Snowden have made surprise appearances at the event.

Aston Villa manager Tim Sherwood will evaluate Gary Gardner during pre-season, as the 22-year-old midfielder returns from a successful loan spell at Nottingham Forest. Gardner expressed his desire to impress Sherwood following his return, and stated that Aston Villa remains his primary club, despite a successful loan period at Forest. Known for his impressive free-kick against Watford, Gardner aims to make an impact at Aston Villa and demonstrated his fondness for Forest as his second-favorite team if loaned again.

A stampede occurred at a nightclub in Santiago, Chile, during a performance by British punk band Doom, leading to the deaths of three people and the injuring of a dozen more, including seven who are in critical condition. The crush outside the Tsunami nightclub caused a structure inside to fall, according to police general Hugo Insulza. The identities of the deceased have not been officially released, but they are believed to be in their 20s and 30s. Authorities have made several arrests in connection with the tragedy, and the band is known for playing Crust Punk songs such as Anti-Social and Raining Napalm.

Bayern Munich advanced to the German Cup semi-finals after a 5-3 penalty shoot-out win over Bayer Leverkusen. Manager Pep Guardiola expressed concern about the team's goal-scoring touch, particularly due to the absences of Franck Ribery (ankle injury) and Arjen Robben (stomach muscle tear). Guardiola acknowledged that the team struggles in one-on-one situations without these players and emphasized the need to adapt their game for the current squad. The team's only goal in their last three matches came from Robert Lewandowski against his former club, Borussia Dortmund. The semi-final rematch with Dortmund is set to take place in the future.

Derry Mathews' world title challenge is in uncertainty as Richard Abril has withdrawn from their fight for a second time, scheduled for April 18 in Liverpool to defend Abril's WBA lightweight belt. If Abril is stripped of his title, Mathews may still fight for the championship in his hometown. Mathews previously defeated Gyorgy Mezei Jnr with a fifth-round knockout on March 6. Abril, who has a history of withdrawing from fights, previously pulled out ahead of the scheduled March 6 bout and has only fought three times since 2012.

1. In a series of humorous videos, English Bulldog Hazel showcases her energetic and curious nature, including attempting to overturn a washing basket and chewing on its rim.
2. The videos of Hazel, which her owner shares on YouTube and Instagram, feature the pup exploring various new things, such as playing on a skateboard, checking her reflection in a mirror, and trying on a collar.
3. Known for her adorable antics and seemingly innocent demeanor, Hazel is a beloved internet personality among dog-lovers.

Catholic bishops in America have criticized the acclaimed BBC series "Wolf Hall" for portraying historical figures, particularly Thomas Cromwell and Thomas More, in a negative light, labeling it as a "prejudice-laden presentation of the past." The drama is said to distort historical facts and present a biased view, with the Catholic News Service characterizing Cromwell as a "monster" and More as an "evidence-flouting caricature." The series, which is based on the Hilary Mantel books and stars Damian Lewis as King Henry VIII, was generally anticipated by U.S. media, but has received some negative reviews, including one in The Washington Post, which warned of a "clear ideological bias" in the adaptation. Despite the criticisms, "Wolf Hall" was hugely popular in the UK, averaging 4.4 million viewers during its six-week run.

Staff Sergeant Shawn Manning, a victim of the 2009 Fort Hood shooting that was ultimately classified as a terrorism attack, claims he is being denied financial support despite being set to receive a Purple Heart medal today. The Army initially denied his claim that his injuries were sustained in the line of duty, citing a 2015 law that does not offer combat benefits for attacks inspired by foreign terrorist organizations. Manning, who is suffering from PTSD and has two bullets still in his body, fears other survivors will face a similar situation, missing out on around $800 a month in benefits. The Army, however, maintains that Purple Heart Medal recipients will receive benefits according to the law. It was confirmed that the attacker, Major Nidal Hasan, had previously exchanged emails with Anwar al-Awlaki, an al-Qaeda spokesman, who later praised Hasan's actions as a heroic act against the U.S.'s war against Islam.

1. John Carver, the head coach of Newcastle United, finds himself under pressure following a series of losses and ongoing fan criticism over Mike Ashley's management of the club.

2. United's supporters are planning to boycott Sunday's home match against Tottenham Hotspur in protest against Ashley's running of the club, citing a lack of investment and ambition.

3. Despite the challenges, Carver maintains that the Newcastle job is the hardest in football due to the criticism he receives, the need for squad overhaul, and the looming possibility of Steve McClaren taking over in the summer, should Derby County be promoted from the Championship.

The 2015 Masters tournament saw a new American golf star rise as Jordan Spieth, aged 21, claimed victory, becoming the first competitor to reach 19 under par in the Masters. Spieth entered the final day with a four-shot lead and comfortably held onto this advantage to secure the title. Born in Dallas, Texas, Spieth gained attention as a teenager, becoming a double US Junior Amateur champion and the sixth youngest player to make the cut at a PGA event. After leaving college early, Spieth quickly rose through the professional ranks, winning the PGA Tour Rookie of the Year award and the John Deere Classic before his 20th birthday. Following his 2014 second-place finish at the Masters, Spieth secured redemption with his 2015 win, which was marked by his famous hug from last year's champion Bubba Watson and a coveted green jacket. His girlfriend, Annie Verret, was on hand to celebrate with him following his triumph.

Beatrice Tollman, a luxury hotel chain founder, donated £20,000 to the Conservative Party for their General Election campaign, but she had previously been charged with tax evasion, although the charges were later dismissed. Her husband, Stanley Tollman, pleaded guilty to tax evasion and had to repay over $100 million. The Tollmans' son also pleaded guilty to tax evasion and was sentenced to prison. These past tax evasion cases may cause embarrassment for Conservative Party leader David Cameron, who has been critical of tax avoidance. The Conservatives have stated they will return donations from the Tollman family in light of these findings.

A 23-year-old marketing coordinator named Poppy Smart complained to police and a construction company after allegedly experiencing a month-long daily ritual of sexual harassment in the form of wolf-whistling and sexist comments from builders on a construction site in Worcester, England. The whistling and comments made her job commute an "awful experience," and she compared it to racial discrimination. Although wolf-whistling is not a specific offense, persistent whistling and obscene comments could potentially be considered a breach of the peace. The builders were working on the expansion of the Bolero restaurant, and the construction company involved, Fimeca, has dealt with the matter internally, with their boss expressing shock and annoyance at his employees' behavior. This incident highlights the issue of street sexual harassment, with Poppy Smart stating that she has been targeted on other occasions in Worcester. The UK government has previously rejected calls to make wolf-whistling illegal, considering it an instance of "everyday sexism" that should be stamped out.

Teenager Lily Sharp in the UK pranked her mother by simulating a kidnapping, referenceing the movie "Taken." Using text messages, she convinced her mother that a stranger was in their home and had kidnapped her, demanding a ransom of £4000. The mother was completely fooled and became increasingly frantic. After sending a picture of herself as proof, Lily revealed the prank, with her mother not finding it amusing. The prank received widespread attention on Twitter.

Bangladesh defeated Pakistan by 79 runs in the first one-day international in Dhaka, with Tamim Iqbal and Mushfiqur Rahim scoring centuries for the hosts. In reply, Pakistan struggled to score, falling short at 250 after Tamim's 132, Mushfiqur's 106, and Wahab Riaz's 4 wickets. Pakistan will aim for a series level in the second ODI on Sunday in Mirpur. The match saw several notable performances, including Azhar Ali's 72 runs as captain, and Arafat Sunny and Taskin Ahmed's three wickets each for Bangladesh.

Todd Kincannon, a 33-year-old attorney and former South Carolina Republican Party executive director, was arrested and charged with criminal domestic violence following an incident with his wife, Ashley Griffith, in March. Griffith reported that Kincannon grabbed her arm, prevented her from exiting the car, and threatened to harm her, himself, and her family. Kincannon claims he accidentally overdosed on prescription medication during the incident, which caused his erratic behavior. Additionally, reports have surfaced of audio recordings and photographic evidence of verbal abuse and possible domestic abuse from Kincannon towards Griffith. In the past, Kincannon has gained notoriety on Twitter for sending inflammatory tweets that have triggered accusations of racism and sexism, including a tweet justifying violence against a woman involved in a high-profile domestic violence case. Following his recent arrest, Kincannon has deleted his Twitter account.

Jordan Spieth, fresh from his Masters victory, is participating in the RBC Heritage Classic this week after a whirlwind media tour in New York. Despite the lack of preparation due to his busy schedule, Spieth is confident about his performance as he chases Rory McIlroy for the world No. 1 spot. Spieth has had success at the Sea Pines Resort in the past, with top-10 finishes, and believes the tournament holds personal significance for him. The RBC Heritage Classic will see a group of top 20 ranked players compete, with defending champion Matt Kuchar returning to defend his title. Spieth, atop the FedEx Cup standings, is driven to continue his pursuit of golfing greatness after his historic Masters win.

Samantha Cameron, the wife of former British Prime Minister David Cameron, demonstrated her appreciation for the alternative group Poliça, known for their psychedelic rock and radical feminist influences. The band, Poliça, whose name roughly translates as 'policy' in Polish, features violent and sexual imagery in their songs and music videos, inspired by Shulamith Firestone, a feminist who advocated for a world without families, childbirth, or gender distinctions. The cover of their latest album, Shulamith, pays homage to Firestone and depicts a naked young woman with blood on her hair and neck. Samantha Cameron attended a Poliça gig in Shoreditch, East London, to show her support for the group.

The Australian government plans to implement goods and services tax (GST) on movie and music downloads, potentially affecting streaming services like Netflix and Apple, as well as online purchases under $1,000 from overseas companies such as Google, Microsoft, Amazon, and eBay. This move is aimed at increasing GST revenue. However, consumer advocacy group Choice suggests tackling domestic costs and access issues for television shows, music, and movies instead. The new tax could lead to minor price increases for Netflix, iTunes, Google Play, Amazon, and Adobe Creative Cloud services. Tech-savvy consumers might circumvent the tax by using virtual private networks to change their location and appear outside the country.

Stephen A. Smith, a host on ESPN's First Take, is facing criticism for his stance on boxer Floyd Mayweather Jr. Smith suggested that Mayweather's domestic violence history should be considered separately from his boxing career. During a discussion about a forthcoming fight between Mayweather and Manny Pacquiao, Smith stated that Cari Champion, a fellow anchor, should feel a certain way about Mayweather's actions due to her being a woman. This statements follows a controversial incident nine months prior where Smith suggested women can contribute to provoking violence. Notably, Mayweather has been convicted twice for domestic violence.

A 12-year-old boy named Mahendra Ahirwar from Madhya Pradesh, India, suffers from a rare condition that causes his head to hang at a 180-degree angle and limits his ability to stand, walk, eat, or use the toilet independently. His parents, who work as laborers, have consulted over 50 doctors but have yet to find a diagnosis or treatment. Despite this, they have expressed their despair and wish for their son to be relieved of his suffering, even if it means losing his life. The community has blamed Mahendra's condition on his father's past sins, causing further distress for the family. Doctors believe Mahendra may have a muscular disorder or spine anomaly, but a conclusive diagnosis requires a thorough investigation. His father remains hopeful for a miracle and desires a normal life for his son.

1. The World Happiness Report 2015 reveals that Switzerland is the world's happiest nation, with strong social bonds, healthy GDP and increased life expectancy being significant factors.
2. Iceland ranks second, experiencing a significant increase in happiness, thanks to factors such as beautiful scenery, cultural history and a perceived sense of generosity.
3. The report finds that Scandinavian nations dominate the top 10, with nations in political unrest or severe poverty being among the least happy. The U.S, despite mocking Canada, ranks lower, while Palestine placed higher than predicted despite conflict.

The upcoming Burnley vs Arsenal Premier League match at Turf Moor will be investigated by Sportsmail, offering team news, provisional squads, betting odds, and Opta stats. Burnley midfielder Matt Taylor is hoping to recover from a seven-and-a-half-month achilles injury layoff to debut against Arsenal, but Dean Marney and Kevin Long remain sidelined with cruciate ligament injuries. Arsenal's Laurent Koscielny and Wojciech Szczesny are facing fitness tests, while Jack Wilshere, Mikel Arteta, Abou Diaby, and Mathieu Debuchy are back in the squad after recovering from injuries. Key stats show that Arsenal has won their last seven premier league games, while Burnley has let in 10 goals in their last four matches against Arsenal in all competitions. Notable players include Danny Ings of Burnley and Olivier Giroud of Arsenal, who has scored in six consecutive PL appearances for the Gunners. The match kicks off at 5:30pm on Sky Sports 1.

The article previews the upcoming Premier League match between Tottenham Hotspur and Aston Villa at White Hart Lane. Tottenham will be without Kyle Walker and Hugo Lloris, with Jan Vertonghen a doubt due to injury and illness. Aston Villa will miss key players Alan Hutton, Ashley Westwood, Scott Sinclair, Carles Gil, and Libor Kozak, but Aly Cissokho might return. Odds for the match favor Tottenham, with key stats indicating that Spurs have a strong recent history against Aston Villa, although Villa's Christian Benteke has been a prolific scorer under Tim Sherwood.

The article previews the upcoming Liverpool vs Newcastle Premier League match at Anfield, providing team news, provisional squads, betting odds, and Opta stats. Mamadou Sakho is unavailable due to a hamstring injury for Liverpool, but Emre Can returns from suspension. Daniel Sturridge and Mario Balotelli may play if fit. Newcastle defender Daryl Janmaat should be fit despite an injury scare. Rolando Aarons and Siem de Jong remain out of action. Key stats include Newcastle's inability to do a league double against Liverpool since 1993-94 and Newcastle's poor defensive record at Anfield. Jordan Henderson has scored in four of his last five Premier League appearances for Liverpool. The match kicks off on Monday at 8pm on Sky Sports 1, with Liverpool favored to win at 4/11, and Newcastle at 17/2.

Nick Clegg, the leader of the Liberal Democrats, has been criticized for blaming various groups instead of himself for the party's declining poll ratings. In an interview with The Economist, he attributed the loss of former supporters to protest voters who deserted the party after it formed a coalition, public sector workers whose pensions were affected and who faced job cuts, and areas that are ideologically opposed to conservative politics. Clegg argued that these factors are more critical than policy decisions he made, specifically on tuition fees. Despite potential losses in the upcoming election, Clegg expressed interest in running the Education department again if his party is part of the next coalition government. Some political sources have characterized his comments as blaming everyone but himself and comparing him to a petulant child.

Chef Bobby Flay's divorce from actress Stephanie March has become more complicated with allegations of a three-year affair between Flay and his assistant Elyse Tirrell. Flay's business partner, however, has dismissed these claims, stating that any ongoing affair with an employee would be known to him. The divorce proceedings have become contentious, with March contesting the prenuptial agreement that stipulates Flay only has to pay her $5,000 per month in alimony. The divorce is getting messy, and there are hints of more accusations to come.

On Saturday night, the Fenerbahce team bus was shot at while on a return journey from an away game in Trabzon, with the bus driver reportedly hit by a bullet. The incident occurred hours after Fenerbahce's 5-1 win over Caykur Rizespor. The bus driver was injured and taken to hospital. The team's striker Moussa Sow contributed to the team's victory, putting Fenerbahce at the top of the Super Lig table. In a separate incident, Caykur Rizespor midfielder Ludovic Obraniak was taken to the hospital with a suspected heart problem, but the initial tests showed he was not in immediate danger.

TV presenter Lisa Oldfield underwent a liposuction procedure to lose weight after her son's unflattering portrait of her prompted her to address her weight concerns. She was motivated to make a change due to her regret of having few pictures with her children and her discomfort with her appearance. The surgery removed 5.5 liters of fat, a cost of $10,000, and Oldfield expects minimal fat to return in areas like her arms. Liposuction won't allow fat to return to the same areas where it was removed.

A couple, Sarah and Mark Brennan, from south Wales, experienced ten miscarriages over a ten-year period yet never lost hope of becoming parents. Last September, Sarah found out she was pregnant, and after some worries, they discovered a strong heartbeat in their daughter Eryn Elisabeth. Born seven weeks early, Eryn was smaller than expected but healthy. Despite some complications during pregnancy and labor, Eryn is now growing well at home after spending three weeks in neonatal care. Sarah advises other couples struggling with infertility not to give up hope.

To commemorate the Football League Awards' 10th anniversary, a team featuring standout players from below England's top tier during the past decade has been assembled. Notable inclusions are Gareth Bale, Wes Morgan, Ashley Williams, Angel Rangel, Adam Lallana, Peter Whittingham, Glenn Murray, Rickie Lambert, Jordan Rhodes, and manager Eddie Howe. Highlighted individuals have demonstrated impressive careers, and some have moved from lower divisions to the Premier League, such as Lallana and Rangel.

Moeen Ali, named as one of Wisden's Five Cricketers of the Year, has recovered from a rib injury faster than anticipated and will join the England squad ahead of the second Test in the Caribbean. He aims to build upon his performances during the World Cup, where he averaged 38 with a strike-rate of 105, and demonstrate his readiness against Australia's left-arm Mitchells (Starc and Johnson) in the upcoming Ashes series. Moeen is focused on improving his ability to face short deliveries and establish himself as the first-choice spinner for the England Test team.

Andy Lee, the current WBO middleweight champion, is preparing for his first title defense against Peter Quillin in New York. Lee and his trainer Adam Booth have made significant improvements in the past year, with Lee expressing confidence in being ready for any challenge Quillin may pose. Quillin, a former champion, is yet to taste defeat as a professional and presents a tough challenge for Lee. Both boxers enter the match with a high level of self-confidence. Quillin believes that this fight will be just another struggle he has to overcome, having faced numerous life struggles in the past.

Usain Bolt is known for his joking and mentorship on the athletic circuit. In a memorable interaction during a World Championships warm-up in Moscow, Bolt playfully made fun of Adam Gemili, a young British athlete, when Gemili was preparing for a 200m race despite being primarily known as a 100m runner. Bolt's humor and advice helped Gemili relax, and he later ran a sub-20 race, with Bolt praising him. Gemili appreciates Bolt's advice on enjoying athletics and not putting undue pressure on oneself. As a sign of this camaraderie within the athletic community, ten British sprinters, including Gemili, posed for a photoshoot. The article emphasizes the ongoing support from players and the National Lottery in promoting sports, arts, and charities in the UK.

Two men, Wade Robson and James Safechuck, who were formerly defenders of Michael Jackson, are set to have their civil claims for sexual abuse heard in court on Tuesday. Robson, now claiming Jackson abused him as a child, and Safechuck, who alleges Jackson performed a secret wedding ceremony with him, missed a statutory deadline for filing their claims. If Judge Beckloff allows their case to proceed, it could potentially lead to further child molestation allegations against Jackson. The estate has contested their claims, arguing that they were filed after the statutory deadline and that Jackson, the only other party with knowledge, is deceased. Both men allege that Jackson abused them multiple times and have provided supporting testimonies from various sources, including a former maid.

A Virginia man, Mark Ward Faville, was convicted of voluntary manslaughter for suffocating his wife Anne in 2000. After the verdict, he took his own life in the courthouse. The couple's daughters testified against Faville, claiming he grew suspicious and followed his wife when she went out. The jury reached a decision in just a few hours, and the incident is now under investigation. Public records and witnesses described Faville's suspicious behaviors in the months leading up to Anne's death.

1. Memphis Grizzlies tied for second seed in the NBA's Southwest Division after a 100-92 win over Oklahoma City Thunder, with Jeff Green scoring 22 points and Marc Gasol adding 19.
2. Dallas Spurs extended their league record of consecutive 50-win seasons to 16 straight with a 123-93 win over Denver Nuggets, thanks to Danny Green's 6-for-6 shooting on 3-pointers, with Kawhi Leonard scoring 20 points.
3. In East playoff-shaping games, Brooklyn Nets won their sixth consecutive game against Toronto Raptors with Deron Williams scoring a season-high 31 points and Brook Lopez adding 30 points and 17 rebounds. Chicago Bulls defeated Detroit Pistons 88-82 with Pau Gasol scoring 26 points and 10 rebounds, and Milwaukee Bucks beat Boston Celtics 110-101, placing a dent in Boston's playoff hopes.

Camellias, known for their polished evergreen foliage and regally beautiful, varied flowers, thrive in acidic, free-draining soil and can be grown in containers if the soil is alkaline or neutral. They are versatile plants that can be grown in pots, pruned to size, and used in various ways, including as hedging or trained on walls. The long-lasting flowers of camellias offer a stunning display throughout winter and spring, with certain varieties like Donation being popular choices. Potted camellias have a lifespan of about five to six years, after which they can be propagated via root cuttings for replacements. The best time to take cuttings is between September and February, while it's also a good time to buy camellia plants for the current season's display. The choice of varieties is vast, with many hardy and attractive options, such as the Williamsii hybrids and Camellia japonica, which thrive in cooler climates. The article discusses the majestic greater adjutant stork, which resides and thrives within the Boragaon landfill in Guwahati, India, known for its vast expanse of fresh waste surrounded by swamplands. The stork, which initially drew photographer Timothy Bouldry to the site, attracted him due to the unique conditions and the resilient community of around 100 families who make a living by sifting through the garbage for valuable scraps. Despite the difficult living conditions without electricity, running water, and sanitation, these families are described as content, loving, hopeful, and spiritual, with a remarkable ability to repurpose their surroundings. Bouldry, who has dedicated seven years to photographing various landfills around the world, has since formed a connection with the Boragaon community and now resides inside the La Chureca landfill in Nicaragua, where he assists the locals in growing gardens from composted waste and teaches English and yoga classes.

A rapist stalked three women in Leeds city centre before attacking an 18-year-old at a bus stop, leaving her with serious injuries and a broken hip. CCTV footage shows the attacker, described as Pakistani or Middle Eastern and wearing a distinctive green Puma hooded jumper, following and approaching potential victims throughout the evening. Police have released CCTV footage, the attacker's description, and a blood-stained rock believed to be the weapon used in the assault in hopes of identifying the man wanted for rape and attempted murder. Investigators suspect the attack may have been premeditated.

A mother of six, named Lizzi Crawford, lost over seven stone after an unexpected comment from a child on a bus mistook her for being pregnant. Crawford, who weighed 20 stone and lived on a diet of burgers, pizzas, kebabs, and alcohol, heard the embarrassing comment and was inspired to change her unhealthy lifestyle, eventually slimming down to 12.5 stone. Crawford's weight loss journey included joining fitness and self-defense classes, cooking healthier meals, and utilizing Hourglass training, a fitness program designed to maintain a woman's curves while she gets healthy. Crawford's support system at the gym, along with her determination, helped her achieve her goal despite facing setbacks such as a cervical cancer diagnosis in 2012.

Nigerian cities, notably Victoria Island in Lagos, have become hubs for luxury goods due to an influx of millionaires, with similar trends observed in Luanda, Dar es Salaam, and Accra. These African metropolises are experiencing growth in the number of ultra-high net worth individuals, changing the landscape of luxury markets. High-end products are no longer concentrated in southern Africa; Nigeria, for example, is now one of the fastest-growing markets for Champagne and digital televisions. Luxury brands enter these markets through distributors to leverage local knowledge while maintaining control over their brand image. Future growth in Africa's luxury market depends on infrastructure development and a favorable operating environment. Home-grown labels also see this as an opportunity to establish a vibrant luxury industry, leveraging Africa's rich cultural heritage and craftsmanship.

Hotel owner Jennifer McGirr, 61, from Blackpool, claims to be living in fear after her hotel windows were smashed and she received intimidating phone calls, following her appearance on Channel 4's 'Four in a Bed.' On the program, she criticized other local hotels as "grim," which led to the window vandalism the following day. The incident was caught on CCTV, showing a man approaching the hotel with a brick, and the abusive phone calls continued with threats and insults. Police are investigating the incident, but no arrests have been made.

Ronnie O'Sullivan, the five-time world snooker champion, dubbed "The Rocket", removed his shoes during a match against debutant Craig Steadman at the Crucible on Tuesday, citing a painful big toe. Despite this, he maintained a 7-2 lead in the first round of the Betfred World Championship. O'Sullivan was given a loan of shoes by tournament director Mike Ganley to adhere to the snooker dress code, as he nearly made a 147 maximum break but missed the 14th red on a run of 104. Meanwhile, Ding Junhui had a chance to make a maximum break at the Crucible but missed after playing for the blue following 12 blacks, while Ali Carter, a two-time Crucible finalist, looked in good form in his first match since being given the all-clear from lung cancer. Mark Allen also won nine consecutive frames from 3-1 down against Ryan Day.

A Sydney teenager, Marian Carole Rees, who went missing 40 years ago while on her way to school, likely ran away and may still be alive, a coronial inquest found. The inquest noted that Marian often discussed running away and had said goodbye to her brother before her disappearance. The inquest also suggested that Marian may have wanted to permanently distance herself from her family and might want to avoid detection. The case has been referred back to the Missing Person's Unit for further investigation due to perceived holes in the initial police investigation. Marian's disappearance is believed to be related to her desire to escape her mother's alcohol-related care responsibilities and run away from her normal life.

A mother employed as an assistant director at a childcare center, Michelle Schwab, has been charged with child endangerment after allegedly dangling her two-year-old son over a 10-foot-deep cheetah enclosure at Cleveland Metroparks Zoo, resulting in the boy falling into the pit. Witnesses reported that the cheetahs did not approach the boy, and his parents leaped into the pit to rescue him. The child suffered minor injuries and is in stable condition. KinderCare, Schwab's employer, has placed her on leave and is investigating the incident further.

A study conducted by researchers at the University of Reading found that chewing gum can help reduce the likelihood and intensity of earworms, or catchy songs that stuck in one's mind. Participants in the study reported thinking about and 'hearing' the catchy tunes less when chewing gum compared to when not chewing or tapping their fingers. The study suggests this technique might also help stop other unwanted thoughts. However, further research is needed to explore this method's potential use in treating obsessive-compulsive disorders and similar conditions.

An Oregon couple, Jesse and Melissa Meek, announced their pregnancy in a creative rap video set to the theme of 'The Fresh Prince of Bel-Air'. The video, which has been viewed over 1.7 million times on YouTube, features the couple rhyming about their life in Oregon, including Melissa's discovery of her pregnancy. The Meeks incorporated elements of the original show, such as admittedly 'living a little lie' about not being ready for children, and the surprise reveal of the pregnancy with a sonogram at the end. The video was made to share the news with distant relatives.

Josiah Duggar, a star from the reality show 19 Kids and Counting, has announced that he has entered into a courtship with 17-year-old Marjorie Jackson. They met while taking Spanish lessons and will follow strict courting rules, including chaperoned dates and saving their first kiss for the wedding day. Marjorie is from a large family and the couple's relationship will likely be chronicled on the Duggar family's reality series, similar to several of Josiah's siblings' relationships. This is the latest in a series of relationship announcements from the Duggar family, following Jessa and her husband Ben Seewald's engagement and subsequent marriage last year. Jill Duggar and her husband Derick Dillard recently welcomed their first child, Israel David, on the same day that Josiah and Marjorie officially started courting.

The Duke and Duchess of Cambridge are about to experience the emotional upheaval of parenthood for a second time. A US-based group of parents has created a viral video, titled "Extra Storage Space," providing advice for new parents. Tips include establishing a schedule, creating time for personal activities, cherishing moments, being grateful, letting children be themselves, being prepared for the unexpected, saving memories, not stressing about chores, and understanding that the love experienced is indescribable. Viewers are encouraged to submit their parenting advice using the hashtag #makeroomforlife.

Arsenal, currently Europe's top form team, is preparing for a Premier League game against Burnley with an unusual pre-game routine. Players have revealed their personalized playlists, with Olivier Giroud choosing Coldplay's 'Every Teardrop Is A Waterfall', Santi Cazorla opting for Spanish pop star Melendi, Nacho Monreal selecting David Guetta's 'Dangerous', and Theo Walcott choosing LL Cool J's 'Loungin'. This light-hearted activity is designed to bring fans closer to their heroes and may contribute to the team's motivation at the upcoming match.

Ed Miliband's US advisor, David Axelrod, who masterminded two presidential election victories for Barack Obama, admitted he pays no tax in Britain on his reported £300,000 salary. He lives and pays taxes in the US, and Labour confirmed they pay him in dollars through his consultancy firm. Axelrod has helped Miliband refine his message regarding cost of living and tax fairness, but his work for Miliband is not mentioned in his autobiography. Axelrod is a political strategist renowned for his role in electing the first black president in the US, although he has had less success in Europe, such as with former Italian prime minister Mario Monti.

In December 2012, Texas Trooper Abraham Martinez followed a motorcyclist, Steven Gaydos, who was driving on a suspended license, engaged in a high-speed chase reaching speeds of 130 mph. During the chase Martinez leaped out of his car and karate-kicked Gaydos, knocking him off his motorcycle, and also fired four shots at him, hitting Gaydos once in the thigh. The unconventional moves led to a three-day, unpaid suspension for Martinez, but the incident was only recently revealed through an investigation by the Austin American Statesman. The shooting and kick, while not specifically violating Texas Department of Public Safety rules, is considered an area needing policy updates according to experts.

In North Charleston, South Carolina, a white police officer, Michael Slager, shot and killed an unarmed black man, Walter Scott, during a traffic stop for a broken taillight. The incident was caught on video showing Slager firing multiple shots at Scott as he ran away, and Slager later claimed he felt threatened. Despite the video evidence, Slager was initially exonerated, but public outcry led to his arrest on murder charges. Despite differences in response between North Charleston and Ferguson officials, both cities have police forces that are not diverse enough to represent their predominantly black populations, and some believe racial profiling played a role in the initial stop. The outcome of Slager's trial remains uncertain.

The article describes a complaint made by Steve Ashton, the son of an 81-year-old woman living in Aneurin Bevan Court sheltered housing, about the quality of meals served to his mother. He was particularly upset about a serving of baked potato and corned beef that he found in his mother's fridge. The meal was reportedly unappetizing, and other meals have been described as undercooked or unpalatable. Ashton is now campaigning for better food standards at the facility, and has already met with Newport City Homes, which oversees the residents' care, to discuss possible improvements. The facility charges £42 a week for food, and residents are provided with two-course meals six days a week and three-course meals on Sundays. Following Ashton's complaint, Newport City Homes has agreed to make improvements and monitor the situation with the family and all residents at Aneurin Bevan Court.

A 71-year-old man named Richard Curry, from Loveclough in Lancashire, had to undergo the removal of his nose due to a rare form of cancer called malignant melanoma in his septum. To keep his prosthetic nose in place, he underwent a series of procedures over the course of a year to have magnetic implants inserted into his cheekbones and nasal cavity at the Royal Blackburn Hospital. Amazed by the success of the operation, Mr. Curry now wears the prosthetic nose all day, removing it at night. A check-up last month showed no signs of the cancer returning. This is a unique case as this was the first time they had used magnets to attach a nose, typically they are used for prosthetic ears.

Jimmy Graham, a new addition to the Seattle Seahawks' offense, is viewed by some as a significant acquisition, but defensive end Michael Bennett has previously criticized Graham, labeling him "soft" and "overrated," and expressing disdain for him as a player and a person following a playoff game two years ago. Despite now being teammates, Bennett has maintained his negative feelings towards Graham and doesn't expect their past rivalry to change their animosity. Additionally, Bennett has denied reports suggesting he's requested a trade to join the Atlanta Falcons.

A woman named Lisa Courtney from Hertfordshire, UK, has the world's largest collection of Pokemon memorabilia, with over 25,000 items amassed over a 17-year period. Her obsession with Pokemon started at the age of nine when she saw a picture of Pikachu in a Nintendo magazine. This collection, which includes cuddly toys, models, clothing, badges, flannels, and posters, has grown so large that her mother had to move from the largest to the smallest room in their house to make room. Lisa's family, despite some sacrifices, has been supportive of her obsession. She travels to Japan to purchase exclusive merchandise, and even considers working at a Pokemon Centre in Japan her dream job. Lisa regularly searches for new Pokemon items online and at car-boot sales to expand her collection.

Raheem Sterling, after rejecting a £100,000-week deal at Liverpool, has been warned by former player Michael Owen that life after the club may not be as desired, as Owen himself moved to Real Madrid, but he isn't good enough for that move according to Owen. Sterling, currently a star player at Liverpool, is being pursued by Chelsea, Arsenal, Man City, among others, but Liverpool are determined to keep him. Owen emphasizes that Sterling is in a great position to develop at Liverpool, but it's not about owing the club anything. He also questions the feasibility of Sterling moving to Spain, with Cristiano Ronaldo and other stars present at Real Madrid and Barcelona, suggesting a sideways move might be the only option if he were to leave Liverpool.

A 26-year-old woman named Natalie Swindells consumes almost exclusively Rice Krispies, avoiding other food items for nearly two decades. Despite her limited diet, she believes it's healthier than overeating other foods and maintains her health. Her dietician suggests she is receiving a balanced diet, but a nutritionist warns that it lacks essential minerals and vitamins. Rice Krispies, a cereal made mainly from toasted rice, contains added sugar, salt, barley malt flavoring, and fortified vitamins and minerals.

George and Amal Clooney are hosting a three-day birthday celebration at their Lake Como mansion for Amal's 37th birthday, which was in February. Notable guests include Matt Damon and Brad Pitt. The event takes place with strict security measures due to local Italian authorities imposing rules for star privacy. Amal is known for her designer wardrobe, as exemplified by her wearing a Stella McCartney sleeveless, embroidery dress at a previous event.

Creflo Dollar, a prosperity gospel pastor, defended his campaign to raise $300 from 200,000 people globally to buy a Gulfstream G650, stating that critics and allegations about his request were attempts by the devil to discredit him. In the past, Dollar had faced criticism for his earlier attempt to raise funds for a Gulfstream G650, which sells for $65 million, due to reports on social media and nationwide media. Dollar claimed the new jet was necessary for his ministry's global travels, citing two accidents in his old plane and the need to provide a luxurious and technologically advanced mode of transportation for his church's 3 million worldwide supporters. Despite the earlier removal of the fundraiser page, donations to the church's gift page are still being accepted.

1. Headmaster Peter Tait of Sherborne Preparatory School in Dorset encourages parents to trust teachers and school staff more, likening current parental involvement to 'dervishes' overbearing in their children's education, due to the continuous influx of advice on raising a child.
2. To avoid hindering their children's natural development, Tait suggests parents should focus on their children's happiness, challenges, purpose, and learning of values, instead of micromanaging their education.
3. The modern trend of persistent parental intervention stemming from excess information and competitive parenting methods has been criticized for negatively impacting teachers' well-being, with reports of parents bullying staff using social media.

An Irish tourist, Barry Lyttle, has pleaded guilty to recklessly causing grievous bodily harm to his brother, Patrick Lyttle, in Sydney, Australia. The incident occurred in January, leaving Patrick in a coma for six days. Despite the initial charge carrying a maximum sentence of 10 years in a district court, the sentencing will now take place in a local court with a potential two-year jail term. The hearing, expected in mid-April, will consider evidence from a criminologist specializing in restorative justice, and may include CCTV footage of the attack. Both brothers have expressed a desire to return to Ireland as soon as possible.

The Ventura County prosecutors have refiled charges against Jane Laut, a woman accused of killing her Olympic medalist husband David Laut in 2009, after a judge denied for the third time a request to delay her trial. This move appears to be an attempt to delay the trial. Jane Laut claims she acted in self-defense, alleging that her abusive husband, who won a bronze medal in the 1984 Olympics, threatened to kill their son and dogs before she took the gun from him. Her attorney criticized the prosecution's decision to refile the charges in a murder case.

A British nuclear submarine, HMS Talent, sustained £500,000 worth of damage in a collision while tracking Russian vessels in the North Sea, potentially in the Arctic Circle, as both countries have increased submarine activity in these areas. The Navy claims the damage was caused by striking 'floating ice', but the incident is under investigation. This incident recalls similar Cold War collisions with Russian subs, such as the 1981 incident involving HMS Sceptre. HMS Talent is currently out of service for repairs and will remain so for several months.

The study found that two cups of coffee daily can potentially reduce by half the risk of breast cancer returning in women undergoing treatment with the drug tamoxifen. This effect is due to coffee's ability to inhibit breast cancer cell growth, especially in combination with tamoxifen. Researchers believe substances like caffeine and caffeic acid in coffee might be responsible for this effect by interfering with hormone-dependent tumor growth signals. This finding suggests that moderate coffee consumption could complement the treatment offered by tamoxifen, but the importance of taking prescribed medication should not be overlooked. Previous research has also linked moderate coffee consumption with reduced risks of liver and skin cancers.

Wild rabbits in greater Sydney are being targeted again for population reduction using carrots laced with a viral disease called Calicivirus, also known as Rabbit haemorrhagic disease (RHD), due to their invasive nature causing damage to agricultural land, native wildlife, and environment. The aim is to reduce the population in May after earlier attempts in March across 160 localities. Pet owners are advised to vaccinate their domestic rabbits to protect them from the virus, which does not affect cats, dogs, or humans. Rabbits, originally brought to Australia by British settlers, can reproduce rapidly and are prevalent throughout the country.

The article discusses the optimism among many Iranians regarding the continuation of nuclear negotiations between Iran and six world powers, known as the "joint comprehensive plan of action." This optimism is based on the belief that a comprehensive deal, expected by the end of June, will guarantee the peaceful nature of Iran's nuclear activities in return for the lifting of sanctions and a return to the international community. This preliminary agreement is seen as a step forward, and many Iranians are hopeful that it will lead to improvements in their lives, particularly in the economy. The stakes are high for President Hassan Rouhani and his "moderate" administration, as this deal could secure their position in upcoming elections in early 2016. The deal is also seen as a historic gesture that represents qualified support for continued diplomacy and international rapprochement, and many Iranians believe that not striking a comprehensive deal would be a historic mistake.

A Sudanese refugee, Mohamed Hamdin, is facing indecent assault charges after allegedly groping a 15-year-old girl at a rap concert in Sydney. The incident occurred during the concert of U.S. rappers YG and Ty Dolla $ign at the Enmore Theatre on Australia Day. Hamdin will reappear in court on April 28. Police records reveal the girl attempted to move away, but Hamdin obstructed her, leading to the inappropriate touching. This incident followed a violent brawl at the concert that resulted in multiple assaults and arrests, including Hamdin's. The rappers, YG and Ty Dolla $ign, have a history of violence at their concerts and suspected gang affiliations.

1. Arsene Wenger is optimistic about Arsenal's title challenge, but emphasizes the importance of maintaining perfection for the rest of the season while waiting for potential slip-ups from Chelsea.
2. Arsenal showed their title contention potential with a 4-1 victory against Liverpool, with goals from Hector Bellerin, Mesut Ozil, Alexis Sanchez, and Olivier Giroud.
3. Despite the impressive win, Wenger offered a cautious optimism, acknowledging their struggle at the beginning of the season due to injuries and late returns of key players, like World Cup winners Ozil and Per Mertesacker. He maintained that, had they been at full strength, they would have been closer to Chelsea in the table.

The article discusses the significant issue of unfilled GP training places, with one in three positions remaining vacant and causing concern for the public's ability to access family doctors. This shortage is attributed to the declining appeal of general practice among junior doctors as they fear overwork, leading to a chronic shortage of doctors nationwide. The figures, from the GP National Recruitment office, indicate vacancy rates as high as 64% in some regions, such as the East Midlands and North East of England, leading to potential recruitment crisis warnings.

Hull KR have signed Australian forward Dane Tilse from Canberra Raiders on a two-and-a-half-year deal to replace Michael Weyman and Ryan Bailey, who recently left the club. Tilse, a former Junior Kangaroo and a two-time ever-present player for the Raiders, has agreed to join the Robins once he receives the necessary paperwork. The signing comes as Hull KR, who secured former England captain Jamie Peacock as their football manager for 2016, look to strengthen their front row after losing both Weyman to injury and Bailey for personal reasons. Tilse is looking forward to the new challenge and the opportunity for a fresh start in Super League.

A 6-year-old girl's teeth were in a dangerous, potentially fatal condition due to her father's negligence, leading to Kenneth Wanamaker Jr's guilty plea for reckless endangerment. He also pleaded guilty to false swearing and faces a two-month to a year prison sentence. The investigation continues into Wanamaker and his partner's connection to the death of other children, including a 7-month-old baby boy in 2011 and two stillborn deliveries since 2007. Despite the ongoing investigation and charges, Wanamaker maintains that he and his partner are raising a healthy, active family.

A 16-year-old transgender boy, feeling like he was living in the wrong body, has been granted permission to undergo male puberty with testosterone injections following a Family Court hearing in Brisbane. The teen, who has previously considered suicide and undergone puberty blockers for a year while wearing a boy's uniform and associating mostly with male friends, was assessed by multiple doctors before being deemed eligible for the treatment. The process of seeking permission from the Family Court for second-stage gender-changing hormones is complex in Australia, requiring a diagnosis of gender dysphoria and demonstrating that the teen's wishes reflect independent choices. While some suggest this process may be unnecessary, it currently exists to ensure the well-being of transgender minors.

A light aircraft, a Piper PA-32, crashed in the Punta Cana region of the Dominican Republic, killing seven people. The foreign office confirmed reports that two British citizens were among the six passengers, but later retracted the statement, stating that early indications suggest no British nationals were involved. The crash occurred during an emergency landing attempt near the Cocotal Golf and Country Club shortly after takeoff from Punta Cana Airport. The Aviation Safety Network confirmed all seven occupants died in the crash.

Cynthia Lennon, who was married to John Lennon from 1962 to 1968 and was the mother of his son, Julian, passed away at the age of 75 on Wednesday due to a short battle with cancer. Cynthia Lennon, originally Cynthia Powell, met John Lennon at art school and was a stabilizing force in his life, particularly given his insecurity following the loss of his mother at a young age. The challenges of John's rising fame, his sometimes-brittle personality, and their eventual divorce marked her life, but she acknowledged the whirlwind as enthralling and that it had drastically changed her life. She is survived by her son.

The stepchildren of Kim Howe, who died in a car crash involving Bruce Jenner, are considering suing Jenner for wrongful death, despite having a virtually non-existent relationship with him. The stepchildren are reportedly looking to prove their case by finding evidence of their relationship with Howe. Jenner, who was not hurt in the incident, is only insured up to $250,000, which could potentially require him to pay from his personal finances if a suit is filed. However, sources close to the investigation suggest that Jenner is unlikely to be charged with manslaughter.

1. Director of the British Museum, Neil MacGregor, announced his decision to step down from the position after 13 years, citing the completion of new building projects and the museum's expansion as contributing factors.
2. Known for his popular book and Radio 4 series, "A History of the World in 100 Objects," inspired by the British Museum collection, MacGregor expressed appreciation for his time at the museum and the opportunities to engage with the collection and colleagues.
3. The museum's chairman, Sir Richard Lambert, praised MacGregor's achievements and expressed gratitude for his contributions, while acknowledging his decision to leave and wishing him success in his future projects. The museum is now seeking a new director to lead the institution in its continued growth and development.

The Augusta National Golf Club has enforced a cell phone ban, leading fans to use old cameras for capturing images of golfers like Tiger Woods during the tournament. Many fans, some not having used their cameras in years, have had to re-learn how to use their equipment. This new method generated comical moments, such as attempts to take selfies with point-and-shoot cameras not designed for such use. Some fans plan to commemorate the experience with photo albums or high-quality prints.

Allie Davis, a 21-year-old Beyonce fan, made her boyfriend take a ten-question exam about Beyonce and other pop stars to stay in the relationship. The boyfriend scored 80% and passed the not-entirely-serious test. Allie shared the results on Twitter, and later shared a blank copy of the exam for her followers to try themselves, stating that it was meant as a joke. Some commentators took the stunt seriously, expressing concern over Allie's behavior. Allie later explained that she made the exam as a joke and to entertain herself.

Ocean photographer Lloyd Meudell, based on the south coast of New South Wales, Australia, captures surreal images of ocean foam explosions on the shore, a phenomenon that resembles froth off a latte or frosted sea-glass. Meudell, who started photography after a lifetime of surfing, uses a Canon EOS 5D Mark III DSLR to achieve these dream-like shots. He advises aspiring photographers to familiarize themselves with the ocean's behavior before diving into the craft, and suggests starting with a GoPro before moving on to more complex equipment.

Bayern Munich suffered a 3-1 defeat in the first leg of their Champions League quarter-final against Porto, with Ricardo Quaresma and Jackson Martinez scoring two early goals and a second-half effort, respectively. Bayern manager Pep Guardiola attributed the loss to the team's current injury woes, while Porto manager Julen Lopetegui expressed optimism about reaching the semi-finals, emphasizing the need for a 'perfect' performance in the return leg. Jackson Martinez, who returned from injury for the match, was a constant thorn in Bayern's defense and played a key role in Porto's victory.

The Curiosity Rover has discovered unique, multi-colored veins on Mars at a site called 'Garden City' on Mount Sharp. These veins, which range up to 6cm in height, are believed to be remnants of Mars' watery past, formed in ancient fluid flows above eroded bedrock. The veins contain both bright and dark minerals, with the darker ones being particularly intriguing to scientists. These findings suggest that Mars once had significantly more water than the Arctic Ocean, possibly enough to support life for over 1.5 billion years. However, over time, Mars has lost 87% of its water, leaving it barren and dry. The study by NASA scientists is the first to estimate the amount of water Mars had in its past, with the arid northern plains containing at least 12.4 million cubic miles of water during the Noachian period. The analysis and exploration of these veins and other layers of Mount Sharp continue, with the hope of uncovering more insights into Mars' history.

A 25-year-old man, Carl Bradey, has been hailed a hero for rescuing a three-year-old girl from a house fire that destroyed his rental property in Palmerston North last month. The fire, caused by a candle, left Bradey with extensive burns across his body, causing nerve damage in his right arm, and he underwent four major surgeries. Currently recovering with his mother, Bradey's family has created a crowdfunding page to aid his recovery and rebuilding process. Fire experts advise caution when using candles, ensuring they are placed on sturdy holders away from inflammable items.

The article reports that thousands of olive trees in the Puglia region of Italy are being destroyed due to a bacterial infection, a move which has alarmed the European Union and led to France boycotting Puglian fruit and vegetables. This action is predicted to lead to olive oil shortages globally, including in Britain, and potentially push prices higher. The destruction of the trees has sparked protests from local growers who believe it will not halt the bacteria's spread. The bacterium, xylella fastidiosa, has already infected over 800,000 trees in Salento, Puglia, and is feared to spread to other regions within Italy and Mediterranean countries if drastic action is not taken. Italy is a significant exporter of olive oil, with major markets including the USA, Japan, China, Canada, Korea, Singapore, Hong Kong, India, and Russia.

In Yemen, a border guard was killed and 10 others were injured in a cross-border fire exchange with militants in Saudi Arabia's Asir region, marking Saudi Arabia's first military death since launching airstrikes against rebels. Meanwhile, Houthi rebels seized the presidential palace in the southern Yemeni port city of Aden. Additionally, reports indicate that Yemeni special forces loyal to former President Ali Abdullah Saleh attempted to secure the city of Aden, while US Navy warships patrol the region, looking for suspicious ships that might be transporting weapons to the Houthis. The situation is complicated, with hospitals struggling to cope and civilians trying to leave the country as fighting intensifies.

Muhammed Tahir, 53, from Leytonstone, east London, was convicted of sexual assault after he intentionally targeted a young woman on the London Underground, rubbing his crotch and pot belly on her bottom. The incident occurred on a busy train during rush hour in July 2021. Detectives found that Tahir had previously been charged with similar offenses in 2003 but was cleared when the prosecution file failed to arrive in court on time.

The judge at the Old Bailey sentenced Tahir to six months in prison suspended for two years, a 12-month supervision order, 150 hours of unpaid work, and an £80 victim surcharge. He was also prohibited from traveling on the London Underground during rush hours for five years. The judge's decision not to jail Tahir immediately was made in the hope that he can address his issues under the supervision of Probation officers. The incident attracted the attention of undercover police officers who were following Tahir's actions.

A Californian man named Robin Barton, who was abandoned as a baby and rescued by retired Santa Ana police officer Michael Buelna from a dumpster 25 years ago, finally met Buelna last week. Barton was adopted by Elizabeth Barton and Daniel Fernandez of Orange County and had a great family. Buelna, who was also abandoned by his mother as a child, shared a special bond with Barton and hopes to help him find his biological mother. Barton wishes to meet his mother to find closure and forgives her for her actions as a young woman in a compromising position. Buelna is content that he got to see the baby boy he saved grow up.

A 16-year-old student, Courtney Brain, visited her GP for a water infection and was given a detention for half an hour of missed lessons. Her mother, Jane Burnham, criticized the school for penalizing Courtney, who has a high academic record and rarely misses school. The school claimed the detention was to give Courtney the best chance at performing well in her exams, but Mrs. Burnham believed the extra half-hour of revision wouldn't significantly impact her overall grades. The school's claim of a 91.2% attendance rate for Courtney was contested by her mother, who stated her daughter's attendance was 98%. The principal of Skegness Academy requested students to make appointments outside school hours or make up missed time.

A 53-year-old former naval serviceman, Graeme Finlay, was acquitted by a jury at Teesside Crown Court of beating two elderly holidaymakers in a dispute over perceived rudeness at a dinner table on a cruise ship, Thomson Celebration. The incident occurred in January 2020, resulting in the elderly couple, Ron Phillips and June Phillips, suffering injuries, including a gash to Mr. Phillips' forehead and Mrs. Phillips' fractured vertebrae. Finlay claimed he acted in self-defense after being hit by Mr. Phillips wielding his crutch. He expressed relief and gratitude following the quick not guilty verdicts for unlawful wounding and inflicting grievous bodily harm. The defense argued that Finlay was shunned by the couple during dinner, leading to a disagreement in the lift later that evening.

American Hayley Carney, a transgender woman, plans to move to the UK to marry a yet-unnamed partner and become a British citizen. She has dreamed of living in Britain since childhood, finding it more accepting of her identity. Hayley will undergo surgery, move to Plymouth, find employment, and follow proper procedures to earn British citizenship, aiming for a long-term stay in the country she has long considered her home.

1. Diego Simeone, Atletico Madrid manager, expressed surprise at the absence of English clubs in the Champions League's last eight, blaming the Premier League's failure to progress in Europe on a combination of player and financial issues.

2. Simeone believes the Spanish league still dominates European football, with Real Madrid and Barcelona being the top two teams, making the upcoming Atletico vs Real Madrid quarter-final match a challenging test for his team.

3. Real Madrid will miss key players Karim Benzema, Gareth Bale, Luka Modric, and Marcelo for the second leg due to injury and suspension, which could potentially benefit Atletico Madrid in their attempt to advance to the semi-finals.

David Cameron and Boris Johnson, known as a potential dream team, struggled with a children's jigsaw puzzle teaching toddlers about seasons in a day nursery during their campaign trail. After facing difficulties completing the puzzle, they resorted to finger painting with Tory blue paint, which they found easier. The visit aimed to promote a Tory pledge to double free childcare for working parents of three and four-year-olds to 30 hours a week.

In a speech at the University of Queensland, Justice Diana Bryant advocated for a reform of Australian surrogacy laws to prevent cases of child abandonment, proposing that commercial surrogacy should be legalized to ensure ethical practices. This suggestion comes in light of international surrogacy cases like that of baby Gammy, where the surrogate mother was left with the child while the parents, who learned of the child's disability, brought home the healthy sibling. Justice Bryant believes that legalizing surrogacy in Australia would provide ethical regulations and protect the rights of both parties involved.

A kitten named Seven, who miraculously survived a seven-story fall in Zetland, inner-east of Sydney, is on the road to recovery. Initially found in a 'terrible state' with severe injuries, including a broken jaw, broken leg, broken hard palate, and bruised lungs, the cat was taken to My Vet Animal Hospital. The clinic shared Seven's story on social media, which led to an outpouring of support from the public. Contributions covered the cat's extensive medical bills and surgeries, and Seven is now ready to find a new loving home in about six weeks.

The TV show MasterChef crowned Simon Wood as its champion, a 38-year-old data manager from Oldham in Greater Manchester. During the final, he impressed judges with a three-course meal, marking the end of the eleventh series on BBC. Kim Woodward, a former MasterChef semi-finalist, made history by becoming the first female head chef at the Savoy Grill, a prestigious restaurant in London that has hosted notable figures since its opening in 1889.

1. Hull City manager Steve Bruce acknowledges the need for "crazy results" to secure Premier League survival, with only a two-point cushion above the relegation zone after five games without a win.
2. Goalkeeper Allan McGregor is under pressure to retain his starting spot following a pair of costly errors in recent matches, with veteran Steve Harper pushing for a recall.
3. Bruce faces a tough challenge in boosting Hull's survival prospects as they face in-form Southampton, who he lauds as one of the best teams outside the traditional "big guns."

Celebrity chef Bobby Flay, worth over $20 million, is reportedly offering his ex-wife Stephanie March, an actress from Law and Order: SVU, $5,000 a month per their prenup, prompting her unhappiness. The prenup also includes a clause allowing Flay to buy out their $8 million marital home for $1 million with an additional $50,000 for moving expenses. The marriage is said to have ended due to Flay's absence during Stephanie's serious health issue, and this is his third divorce. There were previous rumors of a romance between Flay and fellow chef Giada De Laurentiis.

Australian modelling agencies are now prioritizing 'influencers' and 'bloggers' in their model portfolios to meet client demand, as social media influence becomes a key criterion for job bookings. Agencies such as Vivien's Models, Chadwick Models, and Chic Management are creating separate divisions for influencers like Mimi Elashiry and Alexis Ren who have amassed significant followings on platforms like Instagram. These influencers are increasingly sought after by clients for their 'cool girl' appeal and vast social numbers, with the average client expectation ranging from 10,000 to 300,000 followers. To cater to this trend, agencies are also providing social media training to help models self-promote effectively and increase their followers.
