Hungarian architect Matyas Gutai, in collaboration with Milan Berenyi, has developed a prototype house using water as a primary material for temperature regulation. The house, located in Kecskemet, features a water-filled panel system that self-reheats, is energy efficient, and reduces carbon emissions. Gutai's vision aims to redefine the concept of permanence in architecture, promoting a more adaptive and sustainable approach. The system addresses potential issues such as freezing temperatures and panel breakage through inventive solutions like natural solvents and special joint units. The long-term goal is to construct dwellings from this technology, contributing to a greener future.

Cardiff City has decided to forgo the attendance of supporters at their Championship game against Leeds United on Saturday, citing a principle stand in solidarity with a fan-led boycott. This decision follows the Welsh club's dissatisfaction with Leeds offering only 500 tickets to away fans, compared to the 2,200 tickets they offered for the reverse fixture earlier in the season. Leeds United has yet to comment on the matter, and West Yorkshire Police has been criticized for their treatment of away fans in the past. The absence of Cardiff supporters at Elland Road will be a first in recent years for the fixture.

The article discusses Utah photographer Alan Lawrence and his 18-month-old son Wil, who has Down Syndrome. Initially, Lawrence felt negative emotions upon learning about Wil's condition. However, he now acknowledges that Wil brings a joyful energy to the family. Lawrence created a photo series titled 'Wil Can Fly,' in which Wil appears to be flying, using photography editing techniques to remove himself from the images. The series, showcased on his blog and Instagram, has sparked a Kickstarter campaign to donate proceeds to Down Syndrome foundations. Lawrence hopes to increase awareness about Down Syndrome and provide educational content for those without access to proper care through his YouTube channel.

The death sentences of 11 football fans were upheld following a retrial in Egypt over a 2012 stadium riot between Al-Masry and Al-Ahly fans, which resulted in 74 fatalities. The riot erupted after a league match between the two clubs, causing days of protests in Cairo which led to additional casualties. The higher court overturned a previous verdict in the case, ordering a retrial for 73 defendants, which included police officers and officials from Al-Masry club. The court referred the decision to Egypt's supreme court, the Grand Mufti, for a final decision on May 30. The incident was the deadliest football riot in Egypt's history, and authorities have imposed bans on fan attendance and held games behind closed doors to prevent further violence.

In the heart of Nima, a slum in Accra, Ghana, tech entrepreneur Regina Agyare teaches coding to local teenage girls every week at a mosque. She started this coding class in January 2014 as part of her mentorship initiative "Tech Needs Girls," and it has since become a well-established program. The project aims to empower these girls, provide them with education, and offer role models for future generations. Agyare's efforts also include integrating boys in her classes to challenge traditional gender norms and empower them to view women as contributing members of society. The ultimate goal is to help these girls reach their full potential and make a positive impact in their community, though the emphasis is not exclusively on turning them into software developers.

A Wisconsin church's four-decade tradition of mud-wrestling pigs, known as the Original Pig Rassle, has been canceled due to allegations of animal cruelty. The Global Conservation Group, an animal advocacy organization, launched an online petition claiming the event was inhumane and gathered over 81,000 signatures. In response, St. Patrick's Parish in Stephensville announced they will replace the tournament with a human mud foosball tournament during their 45th annual Roundup. The Global Conservation Group considers this decision a victory for their campaign and a significant step forward for animal welfare.

Maria Sharapova has withdrawn from this weekend's Fed Cup semi-final against Germany due to a leg injury, and her last appearance was in the Miami Open at the end of March. Anastasia Myskina, Russia's Fed Cup captain, has to find a replacement for Sharapova, who helped Russia beat Poland in February. In a separate development, Venus Williams has withdrawn from the USA's World Group play-off against Italy due to personal reasons, with Lauren Davis set to replace her on the team. Serena Williams will lead the American team on the red clay at the Circolo Tennis Brindisi.

A 36-year-old woman in police custody is suspected of kidnapping and murdering a 23-year-old mother, Samantha Fleming, in a plot to steal Fleming's newborn baby, Serenity. The suspect posed as a Child Protective Services employee and convinced Fleming to come to Gary, Indiana, where her body was later found wrapped in plastic and doused with bleach. police located Fleming's cell phone signal in Gary, leading them to the suspect's home, where they found Fleming's body. Remarkably, Serenity has been found safe and is now in the care of Fleming's boyfriend and other relatives. The suspect is currently under mental health care in a Texas hospital, with no charges filed as of yet. The suspect was reportedly preparing a nursery at her home in Gary and had claimed to be pregnant with twins.

An Ohio woman, La-Sonya Mitchell-Clark, discovered through newly released birth records that her biological mother, Francine Simmons, works at the same call-center company as she does and lives only six minutes away. After connecting on social media, the two women spoke for the first time, and Mitchell-Clark learned she has three younger biological sisters. The reunion was described as a relief and amazing by Mitchell-Clark's newly found sisters and their mother, who had long wanted to contact her child but didn't know how. Mitchell-Clark's adoptive parents have been supportive of her search for her biological parents.

An Icelandic duo, Búi Bjarmar Aðalsteinsson and Stefán Atli Thoroddsen, have developed a new snack called the Jungle Bar which includes cricket flour, dates, sesame seeds, and chocolate. The bar is high in protein and other nutrients and is vegan, gluten-free, and free from peanuts, dairy, and soy. The duo aims to encourage Western cultures to consume more insects, hoping it can help address nutritional needs and sustainability issues. If you'd like to try the Jungle Bar, you can purchase a box of six through their Kickstarter campaign, with shipping expected in August 2015. The team previously gained attention for their Fly Factory, a micro-factory producing foods using insect larvae, as a potential solution to global food shortages.

A 73-year-old reserve deputy, Robert Charles Bates, accidentally shot and killed Eric Courtney Harris during an undercover drug operation. Bates, who was monitoring the operation from a distance, believed he had a stun gun but instead pulled out his service weapon. Harris was allegedly meeting with undercover deputies to buy a 9 mm semi-automatic pistol and was killed after officers observed him reaching for his waistband, causing concern for their safety. Harris had a history of criminal convictions, including escape from prison, robbery with a dangerous weapon, and making threatening phone calls. Bates, classified as an advanced deputy, has the same powers as paid deputies and can conduct investigations, make arrests, and work on task forces.

A Russian unmanned spacecraft, Progress 59, lost contact with flight controllers during a resupply mission to the International Space Station and is now expected to re-enter Earth's atmosphere between May 5 and May 7, carrying non-critical trash and wastewater. The vehicle's malfunction and subsequent cancellation of the docking plan will not impact the ISS's normal operation or the safety of the six crew members. Roscosmos is currently working on a new resupply launch scheduled for the third quarter of 2023.

Hull City manager Steve Bruce has revealed that players' salaries will be significantly reduced if the team is relegated, with the team currently struggling in 17th place and facing a challenging run-in. The salary cuts are aimed at protecting the club financially, as Hull City has the third-lowest total wage bill in the Premier League. Bruce has praised the recent success of Crystal Palace, but is cautious about expecting an easy match due to Palace's strong finish under Alan Pardew and Tony Pulis. Hull is without several key players due to injury, including Mo Diame, who has been out for five months and is still not 100% fit.

Leo Schofield, a 79-year-old restaurant critic and festival curator, expressed his unhappiest life experience was living in Tasmania for a decade. In a scathing article, he claimed the Tasmanian Government's actions, such as reducing festival funding, caused his mental health to deteriorate, leading him to consider suicide. He labeled Tasmanians as wanting to 'dig it up, chop it down, sell it to the Chinese.' Luke Martin from the Tourism Industry Council of Tasmania refuted Schofield's negative portrayal of the state, asserting that he had been given more funding than requested, and it was his decision to end the festival.

The annual photography competition held by the Northern Territory Cattlemen's Association showcases the unique lifestyle, people, and landscapes of remote Australian regions. Notable winners include Marie Muldoon's heartwarming shot 'True Love', Veronica Elliot's intimate portrait 'Eric', Jacynta Coffey's representational 'Trucking' (2014), and Anna Weir's image of waterlogged farmland 'No.11 Ammaroo'. These photographs highlight the intrinsic bond between humans and animals, the raw realities of rural life, and the impact of nature on regional communities.

The book "Sex by Numbers: What statistics can tell us about sexual behavior" highlights various researches led by David Spielgalhalter, a Cambridge University professor. These studies aim to separate sexual myths from reality. Some findings include the average penis size when erect being around 5.2 inches in length and 4.6 inches in circumference, most men having 7 erections a day with 5 occurring during sleep, and an average amount of ejaculated semen being 3ml. The book also debunks the idea that a larger penis is necessary for great sex.

Barnet secured promotion back to the Football League after a 2-0 victory over Gateshead, with Mauro Vilhete scoring two goals. The victory, in which Barnet dominated, ensured that Martin Allen's fourth spell as manager would be his most successful. Gateshead played well to avoid a heavy defeat, with the match being a potential "banana skin" for Barnet, as a loss or draw would have allowed Bristol Rovers to take their place in the league. The play-offs will be contested by Bristol Rovers, Grimsby Town, Eastleigh, and Forest Green Rovers, while Alfreton, Telford United, Dartford, and Nuneaton were relegated.

A missing college freshoman, Anjelica 'AJ' Hadsell, has been confirmed dead, with human remains found in Franklin, Virginia, around 40 miles from her home in Norfolk. The FBI is involved in the investigation that had initially focused on a pond near Carrville after a tip about her cell phone being in the pond. Hadsell's stepfather, Wesley Hadsell, was arrested for allegedly breaking into a home, though he claims it was out of concern for his missing stepdaughter. The family has expressed frustration with the investigative process, while Hadsell's stepfather has a lengthy criminal history. Hadsell, who stood at 5 feet 6 inches tall and weighed 120 pounds, has gone missing while on spring break from Longwood University.

The article discusses Apple's rumored plans to use stronger materials, specifically 7000 series aluminum, for its next generation iPhone models to prevent issues like 'bend gate' that occurred with the iPhone 6 and iPhone 6 Plus. This material is currently used in the Apple Watch Sport edition and competition bicycles for its durability. The new iPhones, expected to be the iPhone 6S and iPhone 6S Plus, may also include a A9 chip and Force Touch Feature. To minimize the risk of bending in current iPhones, users are advised to avoid carrying the phone sideways in tight pockets, storing it in a shirt pocket or bag, or using a protective case.

The article discusses the current state of European rugby, with Irish and French teams dominating the Heineken Cup since 2007, while no English club has managed to win it since. This season, English sides Northampton, Saracens, Bath, and Wasps find themselves in the last eight of the Champions Cup, but bookmakers favor holders Toulon and Clermont for the title, with Racing and Leinster as secondary contenders. The article highlights several challenges facing English teams, including smaller budgets and past performances, but also emphasizes that teams like Bath and Saracens have proven capabilities, making it possible for one or even two English teams to progress in the tournament. The article provides specific instances of these teams' potential strengths and weaknesses in their upcoming matches.

Sam Pearce, a 24-year-old English teacher from Milton, Massachusetts, was discovered on a New York subway and signed a modeling contract with RED NYC, allowing him to model for top designers like Alexander McQueen and Diesel Black Gold. Despite his fashion career, Pearce prioritizes his teaching responsibilities, ensuring that his modeling events do not interfere with his commitment to his students. He is currently fundraising for new books for his students through DonorsChoose.org, using his modeling fame to generate resources for his classroom.

An amateur astronomer, Gordon Ewen, captured a photograph of a sunspot that resembles a chick sitting on the sun's surface. Sunspots are common, occurring when a concentration of magnetic fields causes a reduction in surface temperature, making them visible. They range in size from 10 to 100,000 miles in diameter and can be seen from Earth without a telescope. Gordon Ewen, a former chemist who recently dedicated his time to astronomy, took the photograph using a telescope in his garden shed in Letchworth, Hertfordshire. Sunspots have temperatures of 2,700 to 4,200°C and are the sources of solar flares and coronal mass ejections, phenomena linked to magnetic fields. Sunspots should not be confused with coronal holes, a different region of the solar corona.

Vladimir Putin is alleged to be preparing to employ nuclear threats and potential cyber attacks, or destabilizing ethnic tensions, to deter NATO from countries bordering Russia, specifically the Baltic states. This includes maintaining control of the Crimean peninsula, considered a flashpoint along with the ongoing conflict in eastern Ukraine. These actions are believed to be imminent due to Russia's perceived aggression towards former Soviet territories, leading to concerns of a potential Russian invasion in the region, with Lithuania reinstating conscription in response. In a separate development, a new clothing label named The Army of Russia has launched in Russia, with designs featuring military apparel and slogans associated with Russia's recent actions in Ukraine.

Virgin Galactic plans to test a new version of SpaceShipTwo by the end of the year, having learned from the 2014 crash that destroyed the previous plane. The new spacecraft is nearly ready for test flights, with construction nearing completion. The crash of SpaceShipTwo led to the death of co-pilot Michael Alsbury and the injury of pilot Peter Siebold, but the company is confident in the safety and improvements of the new spacecraft.

A refugee couple in Cloverdale, Perth, alleges that a neighbor launched a racially-motivated attack on their property, resulting in their children asking if they are truly viewed as "monkeys." The incident, which was captured on video, shows the neighbor verbally abusing the men, brandishing a crowbar, and being physically attacked after charging onto their property. The neighbor, a 51-year-old woman, has been charged with various offenses, but claims she was the victim and insists her country does not welcome people like them. The couple's children are now questioning their identity due to the racist slurs.

Walmart is under investigation following a gun theft incident in Tuscon, Arizona where a thief, Mario Valencia, was able to discharge a stolen rifle soon after leaving the store. Employees claim the rifle was properly locked, but it was later discovered that the wire securing the gun was loose, only wrapped around the barrel and lock once, rather than twice as standard. A police officer, Officer Michael Rapiejko, pursued and ultimately ran over Valencia with his vehicle, causing a violent crash. Valencia was severely injured but survived, facing numerous felony charges for his alleged crime spree, which included theft, vandalism, burglary, home invasion, and car theft. Officer Rapiejko was reinstated after being placed on leave following the incident, as the Pima County Attorney's Office cleared him of any wrongdoing.

A Wisconsin father-of-five, Peter Kelly, was stabbed to death during an argument with three other fishermen at the St Croix River. The argument started when Kelly and a friend asked the other fishermen to quieten down, which escalated over the next three hours. Authorities are searching for the three attackers, believed to be in their late teens or early 20s, and traveling in two vehicles with Minnesota license plates. The small community of St Croix Falls is mourning the loss of Kelly, a volunteer high school wrestling coach, who was known for his dedication to his family and his work.

Holly Willoughby and Davina McCall have teamed up for their first campaign together, endorsing Garnier Nutrisse hair dye. In the campaign, they emphasize finding the perfect shade and show off their glossy locks in a playful photoshoot. Holly has launched a vintage-inspired clothing line for babies, spending 18 months in development for the project. Meanwhile, Davina renewed her wedding vows with her husband of 15 years in Las Vegas, where their children actively participated in the ceremony. The family is currently on a road trip in California.

1. The retirement and subsequent deaths of the baby boom generation are expected to cause a wave of funeral debt due to rising funeral costs and a predicted increase in mortality rates.
2. The report by the International Longevity Centre-UK and OneFamily predicts a 20% increase in deaths in the UK over the next two decades, while funeral costs have risen by 80% over the past 10 years.
3. As funeral costs mount, many families may struggle to pay for burials, with fewer than half of households in the UK reportedly having savings over £3,000, and over one in five families having no savings or cash left by the deceased to help cover funeral costs.

The TSA's Aviation Security Advisory Committee found that full screening of airport employees nationwide would not significantly enhance overall system-wide protection, as it is incapable of determining an individual's intentions to cause harm. The committee recommended strengthening employee vetting, increasing random screening, expanding domestic intelligence collection, and enhancing reward programs for reporting security issues. Following an incident at Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport, TSA Secretary Jeh Johnson announced immediate actions, including strengthened employee vetting and increased random screening.

Raheem Sterling and Jordon Ibe were pictured smoking a shisha pipe together, joining other Premier League stars who have been involved in misbehavior incidents off the field. Notable examples include Jack Wilshere, who has been involved in a smoking row, spitting on a taxi driver while drunk, and holding a shisha pipe during a night out. Diego Maradona was suspended for 15 months in 1991 for a positive cocaine test and later suffered a major heart attack due to long-term alcohol and drug abuse. Saido Berahino was filmed inhaling a legal high while driving, resulting in a ban and fine. Kyle Walker was also pictured inhaling a legal high during a night out, issuing an apology for poor judgment. Robin Friday, a former Reading forward, was known as the original bad boy for his drug-taking, drinking, womanizing, fighting, and smoking despite his talented play, retiring at 25 and dying 13 years later after a heart attack.

The Ask Reddit thread invited members of the disabled community to share their experiences about well-intended actions by able-bodied individuals that are perceived as unsupportive. Many users found statements like "You're so brave" or "strong" insulting, as these comments suggest that their normal activities are extraordinary. Another common grievance highlighted was unwanted help which, although well-intentioned, was seen as infantilizing, especially in the case of wheelchair users. Other complaints involved accusations of faking disabilities for perks, unsolicited diet advice, and the use of religion to explain or console a person's condition. The thread emphasized the importance of understanding and respecting the autonomy of disabled individuals.

A team of German engineers led by DFKI Robotics Center has developed the EOssc2, an innovative micro-car designed for mega cities. It can transform its size, turn on the spot, and move sideways like a crab to navigate tight parking spaces. The vehicle is planned to be semi-autonomous, allowing it to park itself. Currently, it has a top speed of 40mph and is undergoing testing in Bremen, Germany, and Dalian, China, with the aim of creating a car-sharing scheme or energy-saving convoy on highways.

Middlesbrough secured a 2-0 home victory over Rotherham United, with goals from Lee Tomlin and Patrick Bamford in the second half. Tomlin opened the scoring with a clinical finish in the 50th minute, while Bamford doubled the lead six minutes later. Despite the win, Boro remained fourth in the Sky Bet Championship table due to other teams also securing victories. Late in the game, Bamford missed a penalty, preventing him from adding to his 16-goal tally for the season.

A Massachusetts police department, Tewksbury Police Department, was targeted by hackers who encrypted vital records on their computer network, forcing them to pay a $500 Bitcoin ransom to decrypt the files. The malware used was a variant of CryptoLocker, which infected the network through a phishing email. The department lost access to files including arrest logs, motor vehicle records, and calls for service. This is not the first case of a U.S. police department being a victim of ransomware, with similar incidents occurring in Swansea Police Department and Midlothian, Illinois. The Tewksbury Police Department emphasized that this was not a data breach, but an encryption of files that made them unreadable.

A Chinese woman, Zhu Diandian, has garnered internet fame for sharing a close bond with her 187lb pet pig, Five Flowers. She often posts pictures of them sleeping together, walking in the park, and even bathing. The pig is named after Zhu, whose surname sounds like 'pig' in Mandarin, and is reportedly very protective of it. The couple's dog seems jealous of the attention Five Flowers receives. Zhu works in a publishing company and lives in Beijing with her husband, Five Flowers, a dog, and a rabbit. Her pictures of the pig have received numerous comments and over 13,000 'retweets' on Weibo, with many finding it adorable. Some comments suggest not eating pork due to the unusual pet relationship.

A diner, Louise Smith, secretly plucked a young girl's hair and inserted it into her food at the Crown and Thistle pub near Carlisle, Cumbria, in an attempt to get the meal for free. Smith, from Eastriggs, was convicted of fraud this week in her absence. The incident came to light after staff investigated a complaint about a hair in the food under Health and Safety rules, discovering Smith standing over the girl on CCTV footage. An arrest warrant for Smith has been issued, and she will be sentenced at a later date.

Thailand's Kiradech Aphibarnrat clinched his second European Tour title at the inaugural Shenzhen International, edging out Chinese teen prodigy Li Hao-tong in a playoff. Aphibarnrat trailed by two shots with two holes left in regulation, but he holed an 18-foot eagle putt on 17 and narrowly missed a 12-foot birdie putt on 18 to force a playoff. In the playoff, he once again found the same spot on the green and made the birdie putt, while Li missed from a long distance. Aphibarnrat expressed his emotions, dedicating his triumph to his late coach and thanking his mother and caddie for their support. Li, the overnight leader, finished in second place. English player Tommy Fleetwood missed a long birdie putt on the last hole to enter the playoff, ending the tournament in fifth place.

The article discusses two of the most significant fights in boxing history: Floyd Mayweather vs Manny Pacquiao, which is predicted to be the most significant fight this century financially and culturally, and Joe Louis vs Max Schmeling, a political war between America and Germany during World War II. The Louis vs Schmeling fight was notable for its racial and political undertones, as black America saw Louis as a high-profile campaigner for Civil Rights, while Schmeling, who was anti-Nazi, was denied support from his wife and mother due to his loyalty to his Jewish manager. Louis won the rematch in the first round, fracturing Schmeling's spine with his body attacks. After the fight, Louis became a symbol of American strength, while Schmeling, despite being forcibly conscripted into the German army, became a hero in his country for his resistance to Hitler.

The article discusses a new mystery riddle game called None*, available on iOS, Android, and Windows Phone devices. The game presents users with a single clue in the form of a text on a black screen, and a keyboard to type their answers. The clues progress in difficulty from basic maths questions to name associations, cryptic statements, and even coordinates. The game has 50 levels, with 10% of users managing to complete it. The creator of the game, Dimitris Chassapakis, is from Athens and claims this is his first text-based puzzle game for mobile. Some users have found the game enjoyable and are looking forward to the second episode, while others have found it frustratingly vague.

The latest GCSE reform for foreign languages aims to make the learning process more contemporary and engaging by incorporating topics such as tattoos, music festivals, YouTube, and rap music. The new syllabus will include examining a gritty foreign film, analyzing Spanish tweets about the Olympic Games, and discussing radio broadcasts on rap music. The new approach is designed to improve students' linguistic ability and enjoyment, and will be mainly focused on grammar as a crucial toolkit. The new content proposes drawing inspiration from methods used in English as a foreign language, and will potentially include literature extracts. The course is expected to be implemented in schools from 2016.

Danielle Davies, a mother from Morecambe, Lancs, gave birth to Harley, one of Britain's biggest babies, weighing 11lb 5oz, after an eight-hour natural labor without pain relief. Shocked midwives needed to weigh him multiple times because he was too large for their scales. Danielle had a blood clot on her brain a month before delivery, but doctors induced her pregnancy, and she successfully delivered without complications. Baby Harley is now on clexane injections to manage the blood clot and is already in size two diapers.

A couple, Linda and George Hunter, who paid off their mortgage over decades, find themselves in a "ghetto" due to a Liverpool city council scheme that offers neighboring homes for £1. Their home is now estimated to be worth significantly less than its market value, making it difficult to sell. Frustrated with falling property prices and deteriorating conditions in the area, they want the council to reconsider its original offer to buy their home. Liverpool city council defends the scheme, arguing it aims to renovate abandoned properties and transform the area, thereby increasing desirability and property value for existing homeowners.

Celebrities celebrated Easter in various ways similar to the general public, including organizing egg hunts, baking treats, and decorating Easter baskets. Kim Kardashian shared pictures of herself preparing Easter baskets for her daughter North West and possibly her niece Penelope and nephews Mason and Reign. Mariah Carey was seen baking Easter cupcakes for her three-year-old twins Moroccan and Monroe. Amanda Holden hosted an Easter egg hunt for her daughters Hollie and Lexie. Other celebrities like Myleene Klass, Fearne Cotton, Sam Bailey, and Poppy Delevingne also participated in Easter-themed activities with their families.

A convicted fraudster named Gabrielle Yinka Saunders, who had previously been convicted of fraud twice, embezzled £17,000 from her employers, Insight Investments, where she worked as a personal assistant, using company credit cards. The stolen money was used to pay for her wedding, honeymoon, and other personal expenses. Despite her history of fraud, Saunders was spared jail and received a suspended sentence of 15 months' imprisonment, with 200 hours of unpaid work, after she repaid the money and began retraining as a teacher.

A man named PJ Spraggins lost 70lbs in a year to donate his kidney to his wife Tracy, who has Lupus and was on a seven-year-long kidney transplant waitlist. However, due to high blood pressure, they were initially unable to proceed with the surgery. Undeterred, PJ embarked on a rigorous fitness regime to lower his blood pressure, and in December 2014, they got the green light for the operation. The transplant was successful, and both are now recovering at home in Birmingham, Alabama. The couple's friends have set up a fund to support them during their two-month recovery period when they will be unable to work.

A kind-hearted animal lover, Pauline Kidner, is caring for three abandoned badger cubs, two of which were discovered by dogs. The cubs, now named Little Star, Vogue, and Scrumpy, were initially fed milk with a teat on a syringe due to their tiny size, but have since started consuming custard creams to test their readiness for food. As they continue to grow, the plan is to eventually reintroduce them into the wild, ensuring they are vaccinated against Bovine TB and have reduced human contact before release.

Kimi Raikkonen, race-winner in 2007, expressed optimism about Ferrari's chances of winning the 2016 Formula One world title, as he find the current car more suitable and is performing better than in 2014. Despite missing out on a podium finish due to qualifying issues and a late safety car, Raikkonen finished fourth in the Chinese Grand Prix. Raikkonen believes Ferrari can improve, catch up with Mercedes and consistently beat them, but emphasized the necessity of better qualifying performances for a more straightforward race and title contention.

In the article, Stuart McCall, Rangers boss, urges his team to win against Dumbarton on Saturday to maintain their second-place position in the Scottish Championship, as Hibs face Falkirk in the Scottish Cup semi finals. The previous game against bottom side Livingston ended in a 1-1 draw, with Rangers conceding a late equalizer after Myles Hippolyte's goal was initially disallowed for a foul. Livingston's manager, Mark Burchill, felt his team could've won the game, as Rangers didn't play their best.

Nigel Farage, the Ukip leader, plans to use a speech at the European Parliament in Strasbourg to warn that allowing refugees from North Africa into Europe could provide a cover for Islamic extremists, potentially leading to millions of migrants being given passports that could allow them to move to Britain. Farage believes that this could be more damaging than the eurozone crisis, and his speech may be his last in the European Parliament if he is elected as an MP for Thanet South. In a separate development, during a campaign visit to Hartlepool, Farage accused the SNP of being "openly racist."

Kai Windsor, a 10-year-old boy, was born as a girl but identified as a boy since the age of three. He preferred playing football over dolls and showing boyish behavior. His mother Rachel, a single mother from Cheltenham, noticed his discomfort around girls and his preference for boy's clothes. Kai faced gender issues which have quadrupled in referrals to the NHS since 2009. His primary school provided him with counseling and explained his condition to his classmates, also planning to build unisex toilets for his convenience. Kai is now set to undergo hormone treatment to halt puberty and is scheduled for gender reassignment surgery if he chooses to transition fully at the age of 16.

A Hawaiian fisherman, Ron Ingraham, aged 67, is missing after his boat ran aground on rocks near Hawaii's Lanai island following a severe storm, just a few months after he was rescued following a 12-day ordeal lost at sea. His sailing mate, Kenny Corder, survived the incident and claims to have left Ingraham with a life ring to swim back to the boat and radio for help, but Ingraham was nowhere to be found upon Corder's return. This event renews concerns for Ingraham's safety, and a search is currently being conducted by the U.S. Coast Guard. The incident marks the second major difficulty at sea for Ingraham within six months.

A father and son, Nicholas Pence (25) and David Pence (56), were shot dead in an apparent execution-style murder in their home in Metairie, New Orleans, after celebrating a victorious football game. The police have arrested two suspects, Dexter Allen (17) and Haraqyon Degruy (18), who reportedly have no significant criminal history. The motive and connection between the suspects and victims remain unknown. The community is shocked and saddened by the incident, describing the victims as outgoing and lively neighbors. The investigation is ongoing.

June Whitfield, known for her role as Edna's mother in Absolutely Fabulous, is set to play a nun, Sister Ruth, in EastEnders. In this role, she will provide advice to Kat Moon (Jessie Wallace), who is grappling with the aftermath of childhood sexual abuse. Whitfield expressed joy at working with Wallace and stated that she has long admired EastEnders for its acting standards. The inclusion of older characters in soap operas has been a topic of conversation recently, with Timothy West criticizing the underrepresentation of older characters, and Linda Marlow, another older actress, joining the EastEnders' cast.

Lewis Hamilton, a Formula One racer, tops the 2015 Sunday Times Sport Rich List with a fortune of £88 million. Wayne Rooney, a Manchester United and England football captain, has moved up to second place with a wealth of £72 million, a significant increase of £12 million from the previous year. Andy Murray, a tennis player, holds the fourth position on the list with a wealth of £48 million, due in part to new deals with Standard Life and Under Armour.

Researchers at Yahoo Labs have developed a sensor technology called Bodyprint that uses a touchscreen to scan body parts, such as ears, fingers, fists, and palms, as a means of biometric identification for smartphone and tablet access. The technology is designed to improve convenience and security by eliminating the need for fingerprint readers or infrared cameras, while also providing a high level of accuracy during tests. The goal is to make Bodyprint available to smartphone manufacturers in the future.

1. A woman named Belinda, 56, from Essex, suffered horrendous scars around her ears from a botched facelift performed in Turkey, leaving her feeling worse than before.
2. Belinda had the surgery due to being self-conscious about her appearance, opting for the cheaper option offered overseas despite the risks.
3. After discussing her case on TLC's Extreme Beauty Disasters, Belinda underwent corrective surgery by plastic surgeon consultant Vik Vijh, who aimed to lift her neck, pull up her face, and remove scarring. The new procedure has improved her confidence and made her happy with her new appearance.

Chuka Umunna, the shadow business secretary, accused UKIP leader Nigel Farage of having a "problem with race" due to his remarks about "fully black" and "half black" UKIP supporters and the presence of far-right supporters at a UKIP event in South Thanet. Umunna claims UKIP whips up anti-immigration sentiment, is infected with the "virus of racism," and fails to deal with it due to Farage's stance on equalities legislation. Umunna believes UKIP does not like modern Britain and blames immigrants for the country's problems, comparing their actions to those towards black and Asian people in the 1960s and 1970s.

Model Maggie Rizer, 37, has returned to her fit physique just nine weeks after giving birth to her third child, daughter Cecilia Kathryn. She showcased her toned figure in a string bikini while playing with her two-year-old son Quinnlann Clancy on the beach, which she shared on Instagram. Online commenters praised her quick post-pregnancy transformation. Despite taking care in selecting her shared images, some followers complimented her on her remarkable body recovery, attributing it to her hard work, particularly her Pilates routine. Maggie maintains a profile on social media, sharing family moments with her husband, Alex Mehran, and their three children.

The article presents a survey revealing that British people eat an average of four servings of cheese a week, with cheddar being the favorite variety. The survey also found that many Brits enjoy cheese with pickles and consider cheese sandwiches as a comfort food. Another survey showed that a significant number of office workers in Britain have been eating the same lunch for nearly four and a half years on average. The article suggests trying out different recipes such as chicken and mango sandwich with mint raita, smoked ham and egg with capers, gherkins, and mustard mayo, and feta with avocado and roasted red pepper for diversity in meals.

A dress worn by Vivien Leigh in the 1939 movie Gone With the Wind, featuring a black zigzag applique, fetched $137,000 at auction. The dress, originally a slate blue-gray, has faded to light gray over the years. The dress, one of more than 150 items from the film, was part of the private collection of James Tumblin, a former hair and makeup department head at Universal Studios. The auction also saw a straw hat worn by Leigh sell for $52,500, a suit worn by Clark Gable sell for $55,000, and a black bonnet worn by Leigh and Olivia De Havilland sell for $30,000.

A Turkish Airlines flight from Milan to Istanbul made an emergency landing at Ataturk Airport today due to its engine catching fire, marking the latest in a series of such incidents for the carrier. The incident forced the pilot to abort a first landing attempt, and upon a second attempt, the right landing gear collapsed. The plane safely evacuated all 97 passengers, and no injuries have been reported. The plane ended up on the grass after the emergency landing, and the fire was extinguished on landing. This incident follows two recent bomb threats on Turkish Airlines flights out of Istanbul.

Adam Leheup, a 34-year-old architect, was acquitted of rape and sexual assault charges at Blackfriars Crown Court. He had been accused of forcing himself on a woman he met on a dating app, with the alleged incident taking place hours after their first meeting. During the trial, Leheup claimed the woman 'freaked out' when he tried to comfort her about her saggy breasts, and he had denied having non-consensual sex. Leheup, who admitted to communicating with thirty-five women and having sex with six of them, was emotional after being cleared of the charges following a week-long trial.

Italian activist and artist AleXsandro Palombo has launched a campaign, #briefmessage, encouraging women to write their thoughts on gender violence on their underwear and share them via social media in a bid to challenge machismo. The responses, written in a mix of English and Italian, range from defiant messages to simple statements like "I'm not an object, I'm a subject." Many men have also joined the campaign by holding up their pants with phrases like "I'm a feminist" to support the cause. Palombo hopes the campaign will spark a broader discourse about gender violence and encourage both men and women to take a stand against it.

Nick Clegg faced opposition from tuition fee protesters in Surbiton, London, as he criticized George Osborne's budget plans. Clegg warned that Osborne is "a very dangerous man" whose ideological approach would cause significant damage to the economy, particularly affecting the working poor. In a separate incident, Treasury Secretary Danny Alexander accused top Tories of hypocrisy for prioritizing tax cuts for the wealthy, while publicly advocating for tax increases for the general public.

Sharon Edwards, a 55-year-old teacher, has been missing since March 14 in Grafton, NSW. Her car and clothing were found at home, but her wallet, handbag, and car keys are missing. Her family, including her husband and three sons, are struggling with her disappearance and are concerned due to it being out of character. Police are treating the investigation as a homicide due to a lack of history of mental illness, but there are no known enemies or theories about her disappearance. The community is being urged to provide any information regarding her whereabouts to the Grafton Police Station or Crime Stoppers.

The article discusses a husband's heartfelt essay appreciating his wife's role as a stay-at-home mother to their two-year-old son. Contrary to the title, he indicates he can't afford for her to stay home due to high childcare costs and the financial value of the various domestic tasks she performs. He estimates her annual "salary" to be approximately $73,960, which he feels he fails to fully provide as her income doesn't cover her contributions to the family. The husband, Steven Nelms, ends the essay by telling his wife she is more valuable than rubies.

Prime Minister David Cameron on Thursday defended his election campaign, vowing to continue warning about Labour's economic threat and focusing on issues like jobs, business, and childcare. Tory donors and figures have criticized the campaign for a lackluster message and failing to pull away in the polls. A potential leadership coup against Cameron is being discussed among some MPs, with Boris Johnson being suggested as a possible replacement. Criticisms include Cameron's lack of energy, the need for a clear vision of the future, and the belief that his economic stewardship message may not be enough to win the election.

Two former Parma, Missouri police officials, Trish Cohen and Rich Medley, resigned from their positions following the election of Tyus Byrd, a black woman, as the town's mayor. Cohen and Medley allege that their home addresses were shared online by Byrd's family members, causing them to fear for their safety. Byrd, who denies any knowledge of these safety issues, also claims that race was not a factor in the resignations. In response to their resignations, six city officials quit their jobs shortly after Byrd was elected.

Johan Bavman, a photographer from Sweden, undertook a project to document fathers utilizing their country's offered parental leave, which allows for a total of 480 days, with 390 paid at 80% of income. To ensure equal parental involvement, Sweden mandates that 60 days be designated as "daddy months" or "partner months." Despite Sweden's policy promoting shared parenting, mainly women act as the stay-at-home parent, while men continue to prioritize their careers. Bavman photographed several fathers who utilized their full parental leave, capturing their dedication and real-life experiences, while also highlighting the difficulties and challenges of full-time parenthood. The project aims to showcase these fathers as role models and inspire others to reconsider their priorities and potentially make career changes.

The article discusses the tragic drowning of twin 18-month-old boys, Eli and Silas Keslar, in a canal in Yuma, Arizona. Their mother, Alexis Keslar, was attempting to swat away a bee and lost grip of their stroller, which rolled into the canal. Despite her efforts to rescue them, the steep banks proved too difficult to navigate, and she was unable to save her sons as they were swept away by the strong current. Authorities and family friends have expressed their condolences, with a GoFundMe page being set up to cover memorial and medical costs. The incident serves as a warning about the potential dangers of canals that may not appear to be harmful.

1. Arsene Wenger has not made a decision about offering Abou Diaby a new contract, but suggests the injury-prone midfielder could remain at Arsenal beyond this summer. Diaby returned from his latest injury in a practice game on Wednesday.

2. Wenger also hopes to extend contracts for captain Mikel Arteta and long-term midfielder Tomas Rosicky, who have been out with injuries. Diaby, since joining Arsenal in 2006, has suffered a total of 42 injuries over the years.

3. Diaby has played only 67 minutes this season and Wenger has hinted that any new offer for Diaby could be on a pay-as-you-play basis, subject to him demonstrating his consistency.

1. Eden Hazard, considered the best player in the Premier League this season, demonstrated his importance to Chelsea's imminent title victory by scoring the only goal in their 1-0 win over Manchester United, boosting his season tally to 17 goals.

2. Hazard's growth as a player has been evident not just in his creative abilities but also in his finishing, which has become critical in securing wins for Chelsea even when the team is not at its best.

3. With Chelsea relying on Hazard's contributions to find the crucial goals, the Belgian has proven himself as a vital player who can contribute defensively when required, and is now closing in on being a top-three player in the world, with the potential to reach that level if Chelsea can make a Champions League final.

1. At the Summit of the Americas in Panama City, President Obama met with Cuban leader Raul Castro for the first high-level conversation between their nations in over 50 years, marking a historical milestone in normalized relations.
2. The United States is expected to remove Cuba from its list of countries that sponsor terrorism, signifying a major advance in diplomatic ties.
3. Tensions remain domestically and internationally around the diplomatic overtures, with some U.S. lawmakers and dissidents in Cuba criticizing the pace of human rights reforms and engagement with the Cuban government.

A woman, Latisha Fisher, has been charged with second-degree murder after allegedly smothering her 20-month-old son Gavriel Ortiz in a bathroom at a Manhattan restaurant. Fisher reportedly told police she did so to protect him from being eaten by someone, stating she put him to sleep. Previously, Fisher had a history of psychiatric problems, including a diagnosis of schizophrenia following a 2011 stabbing incident. Despite this, she was evaluated as mentally fit as recently as last year and received positive evaluations afterward, leading to a probation sentence for the stabbing incident. Witnesses reported Fisher as emotionless following the death of her son and that she had indicated she believed the devil was responsible.

1. The Star Wars: Episode VII - The Force Awakens panel at California's Anaheim Convention Center featured Carrie Fisher and Mark Hamill, with Harrison Ford absent due to recovery from a plane crash. Producer Kathleen Kennedy announced Ford was resting and would return to work soon.

2. During the panel, Kennedy and director JJ Abrams discussed Ford's emergency landing and referred to him as a real hero. The second trailer for the film was released, featuring the return of characters such as Han Solo, Chewbacca, and R2-D2, as well as new faces like John Boyega and Daisy Ridley.

3. The panel included the presentation of new scenes from the film, as well as discussions about the production process, the characters' development, and the return of classic elements such as the Millennium Falcon and the use of practical effects over CGI.

Bill Nye, the television personality known as "the Science Guy," joined President Barack Obama for an Earth Day excursion to the Florida Everglades, aboard Air Force One. In a seeming contradiction to his environmental activism, Nye expressed his love for the smell of jet fuel before boarding the plane. The trip, a 1,836-mile round trip, resulted in the jet's emissions of more than 9,180 gallons of fuel. Obama used the visit to promote his administration's commitment to reducing carbon pollution and preserving wetlands. Some critics pointed out the apparent irony of Obama's greenhouse gas message amidst his own travel-induced emissions.

Floyd Mayweather Jnr, the boxer, recounts how he told his friends he would make over $100 million in one night, which was met with disbelief. He broke away from Bob Arum, the promoter, to become an independent boxing businessman. This decision led to the richest fight in boxing history against Manny Pacquiao, where both fighters will earn over $100 million. Mayweather takes pride in being his own boss and dictating the timing of this fight, with the world eagerly awaiting their collision. Over two weeks before the fight, Mayweather was working out at his Las Vegas gym, flanked by his team and family. He is confident about the fight, suspecting Pacquiao has a neurosis about being the smaller man, leading him to wear lifts in his shoes. Mayweather arrived for this workout in his new Mercedes Party Bus and was followed by his girlfriend in a Rolls Bentley. Despite the heavy security and media attention, Mayweather remains calm, viewing this as just another fight in his career. After this fight, Mayweather plans to fulfill the last fight of his contract at the MGM Grand in September.

Elderflower Fields, a family-oriented festival held in Pippingford Park, offers a blend of outdoor activities, luxury experiences, and emphasis on children's development in various areas such as music, sports, arts, and environment. The festival features live performances, workshops, and interactive activities catering to different age groups. Notable attractions include the Sports camps by Premier Sports, Urban Woods, and and So Sussex Sunday picnic. Tickets are available at elderflowerfields.co.uk, with adult weekend tickets priced at £95, child weekend tickets at £45, and under 5s entering for free.

The Professional Footballers' Association (PFA) Premier League team of the year for the 2014-15 season was announced, with Chelsea having six players selected. The team includes Jose Mourinho's men's entire back four, with center-back pair John Terry and Gary Cahill joined by Branislav Ivanovic and Ryan Bertrand. Midfielders Eden Hazard, Nemanja Matic, Philippe Coutinho, and Alexis Sanchez were also selected. Tottenham forward Harry Kane and Chelsea's Diego Costa were chosen as the forwards. Manchester United goalkeeper David de Gea, who has made 10 clean sheets this season, received the goalkeeper spot. Notably absent from the team is Chelsea's Cesc Fabregas, who has made 16 league assists this season.

A 21-year-old father named Michael Owen, who had recently received a job offer and was preparing for his daughter's fifth birthday, tragically died along with his friend Kyle Careford in a road accident in East Sussex. The men's Renault Clio crashed into a church wall in Crowborough, leaving skid marks and a significant gap in the sandstone wall. Tributes and condolences have been shared for the two young men, with family and friends expressing their love and grief for the losses. Michael Owen, a father to Lily-Rose Iris, was remembered as a responsible and loving parent. Kyle Careford was thought to have died just days before his 21st birthday. The investigation into the cause of the accident is ongoing, with police urging witness accounts.

The article discusses the discord between Manchester City's supporters and the current state of the team, with some wanting a return to the "old City." Celebrity fan Ricky Hatton and musician Noel Gallagher express apathy towards the Champions League among the fans. Manager Manuel Pellegrini's position is under scrutiny after losing to their rivals, with criticism over his lack of ability to motivate the team and make significant signings. Notable examples of underwhelming signings are Jesus Navas and Cesc Fabregas, who could have provided much-needed improvement to the side. Some suggest replacing Pellegrini with managers like Diego Simeone, Jurgen Klopp, Carlo Ancelotti, or Pep Guardiola who have shown potential for greatness. The article ends with a call for City to think bigger and aim for dominance in both the Premier League and Champions League.

A 39-year-old Irish mother of two, Kim Callaghan, lost over ten stone after feeling her size was causing her to look masculine. Worried about her shape and losing her femininity, she adopted a diet and exercise routine that led to a decrease in her weight from 20st 3lb to 9st 10lb. As a result, Kim, who is now a size eight, feels confident enough to wear dresses and has a more feminine appearance compared to her previous wardrobe of masculine clothing. Kim's weight loss occurred through swapping starchy meals for smaller portions and participating in regular exercise such as cycling, and she has successfully maintained her new lifestyle for several years.

In Miami, a police investigation revealed baggage handlers at Miami International Airport have been going on shopping sprees with passengers' luggage, unknowingly being recorded by hidden cameras. This is part of an ongoing issue of insider theft at the airport, which is one of several airports in the U.S. with reported cases of stolen valuables from luggage. The Miami-Dade Police Department and other authorities have been actively investigating and arresting those involved in these thefts, but the problem persists. The total claimed property loss from these incidents from 2010 to 2014 was $2.5 million, with John F. Kennedy International Airport in New York experiencing the most reported thefts. Similar cases have been reported at other airports, raising concerns about potential links between luggage theft and more serious issues like terrorism.

Marla McCants, a woman who weighed 800lbs due to a spiraling weight gain after being kidnapped and held hostage, managed to stand for the first time in years. Initially, she refused to cooperate with medical professionals following a gastric bypass surgery, leading to a lengthy hospital stay. However, realizing her life was at risk if she remained bedridden, Marla attempted to stand with the help of a walker, Dr. Younan Nowzaradan, Emergency Medical Technicians, and her daughter Sierra. This short moment of standing proved to be crucial, boosting her confidence and significantly improving the direction of her recovery.

1. New findings from Nasa's Mars rover Curiosity suggest there might be liquid water close to the surface of Mars, especially in the Gale Crater, where the soil contains the substance perchlorate that lowers the freezing point.
2. The Gale Crater, with its large lake and sedimentary deposits, appears to have been a giant lake on Mars in its past, and evidence of water on Mars dates back to the 1970s.
3. The area exhibits signs of old riverbeds, and the new findings could potentially make it easier for humans to live on Mars in the future, although the current environment might be too harsh for known forms of life.

1. The police are still searching for an 11-year-old autistic boy named Luke Shambrook who went missing from a campsite in Victoria on Good Friday. The search is ongoing in the thick bushland areas around Lake Eildon, with an increased number of police, emergency and volunteer crews participating.

2. It is believed that Luke may have been seen walking near the Devils River, four kilometers south of his campsite, and a sighting of a young boy matching his description was reported by a family driving in that vicinity. Search crews have rushed to the location, and there is hope that Luke is still alive.

3. With cold temperatures dropping to as low as eight degrees Celsius, Senior Sergeant Ralph Willingham believes that the fourth day of searching will have a further level of urgency. The family, campers, and search teams are working together in the search efforts, and Luke is described as being of medium build, about 150 cm tall with olive skin, brown hair, and brown eyes, last seen wearing a black windcheater, black t-shirt, grey track-pants, grey boots, and a scarf.

Nicola Sturgeon, Scotland's First Minister, has voiced her support for transferring all tax powers to Holyrood, a move that could result in a budget deficit of £7.6 billion. This deficit could lead to increased taxes, spending cuts, or unsustainable borrowing levels. During a televised election debate, Sturgeon circumstances under which she would support another independence referendum. Jim Murphy, the Labour leader, warned that pursuing fiscal autonomy would create a catastrophic budget hole in Scotland. The debate focused on the SNP's push for 'full fiscal autonomy,' a move that could impact Scotland's economy significantly as North Sea oil revenues plummet.

The Royal Commission into Institutional Responses to Child Sex Abuse in Rockhampton, Queensland, has heard harrowing accounts of abuse suffered by victims at the Neerkol orphanage, operated by nuns and priests, where allegations include gang rapes, forced urine consumption, and rape using a broom handle. AYL, a victim who was sent to the orphanage in 1961, claimed she was routinely raped by a male employee, gang raped at one point, and raped with a broom handle on one occasion. Other former residents also reported emotional, physical, and sexual abuse. Bishop Brian Heenan, a former Catholic bishop of the Rockhampton Diocese, has been accused of being dismissive and failing to identify a priest who sexually assaulted a victim. The commission is expected to continue until April 24, and many former residents of Neerkol have come forward with their stories of abuse.

The Kentucky Derby at Churchill Downs, scheduled for May 2nd, has banned selfie sticks due to safety concerns for both the horses and the large crowd. This follows similar bans at music festivals such as Coachella and Lollapalooza, as well as at museums like the Smithsonian and the National Gallery of Art. The ban doesn't eliminate the ability to take selfies, but limits the reach of the photos to the length of one's arms. Churchill Downs encourages social media attention and creativity, but this measure is intended to ensure safety.

The Mercedes-Benz Fashion Week Australia (MBFWA) concluded on Thursday, with Johanna Johnson's Hollywood-inspired Sirens' Call presentation bringing the event to a close. The week featured trends such as voluminous silhouettes, metallics, and flimsy, sheer fabrics. Some shows included intricate detailing and couture masterpieces, while others showcased bizarre beauty looks and trends that might not be attempted in real life. Notable trends included face bling, gladiator sandals, and out-there headwear. The week also included comments on fashion industry issues, such as diverse body types and bringing children to shows.

Prince William, who recently began working as a pilot for East Anglian Air Ambulance, plans to take two weeks of paternity leave when his second child is born later in April. The Duke and Duchess of Cambridge, who are expecting their second child, have requested privacy for the birth and prefer to minimize any media attention or public gatherings. The Duchess, who will give birth at the Lindo Wing of St Mary's Hospital in London, has not yet specified how much maternity leave she plans to take. The couple has expressed gratitude for the warm wishes they have received from around the world in anticipation of their new baby.

Leanne Kenny, a 23-year-old woman from Northwich, Cheshire, lost seven stone after realizing her unhealthy habit of taking home discounted junk food from her job at a supermarket was contributing to her weight gain. Apple has acquired LinX Computational Imaging, an Israeli company that specializes in making multi-aperture cameras with depth-sensing technology. These compact cameras can sense the depth of objects in photographs, allowing for post-capture refocusing and room dimension measurement. This technology could be integrated into future iPhone and iPad models. LinX's cameras are significantly smaller than existing models on the market, approaching DSLR performance in portable devices. The HTC One M8 already incorporates a similar technology in its Duo Camera, offering editing options like Ufocus, Foregrounder, Seasons, and Dimension Plus. Apple's acquisition of LinX confirms its focus on improved camera technology for its devices, as shown in its recent marketing campaign for the iPhone 6 series. A recent patent awarded to Apple also describes a three-sensor camera that splits incoming light into three components (green, red, and blue) before projecting them onto three separate sensors. This could potentially improve image quality, especially color vividness and sharpness, by using more pixels per photo. The technology is similar to what is found in professional cameras and includes stabilization to accommodate hand shaking.

The Moai statues of Easter Island, known for their distinctive red "hats" or "pukao," have been studied for centuries. Experts now believe that these heavy red stones, weighing up to 12 tonnes, were rolled up ramps to reach the tops of the 40ft tall figures. A team of researchers, including Sean Hixon, suggest that a relatively small group of people could have accomplished this task. The 1,000 carved Moai line the perimeter of the volcanic Easter Island, the most isolated inhabited landmass on Earth with just 6,000 residents. These statues, created by the Rapa Nui people between 1,250 and 1,500 AD, symbolize power and authority and are believed to represent deified ancestors keeping watch over the villages. The exact method of transporting these vast statues, including their "hats," has remained a mystery, as the island is half the size of the Isle of Wight. This latest study points to the possibility of ramps as the solution, but acknowledges that more analysis is needed to reach a definitive conclusion.
